Explanation: Edges are the connections in a Microsoft Agent Framework workflow graph that route messages between executors, and they can be direct, conditional (routed only when a condition is true), switch-case, fan-out (one source to many targets) or fan-in (many sources to one target). Executors are the processing units, either agents or custom functions, that receive typed messages, do work and send outputs or events. A WorkflowBuilder assembles executors and edges, and the runtime executes the graph in supersteps, a bulk synchronous model in which messages are delivered and processed in rounds. Workflows emit events for observability, support checkpoints and human input, and can be defined in code or declaratively in YAML.
trans_Question: ɪn ə májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk wɜ́rkflòw, wɪ́tʃ kəmpównənt dɪfájnz háw mɛ́sɪdʒɪz flów bɪtwíjn prɒ́sɛsɪŋ júwnɪts, ɪnklúwdɪŋ kəndɪ́ʃənəl ənd fǽn-áwt ráwtɪŋ?
trans_Explanation: ɛ́dʒɪz ɑr ðə kənɛ́kʃənz ɪn ə májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk wɜ́rkflòw ɡrǽf ðæt rúwt mɛ́sɪdʒɪz bɪtwíjn ɪɡzɛ́kjətərz, ənd ðej kən bij dɪrɛ́kt, kəndɪ́ʃənəl (rúwtɪd ównlij wɛ́n ə kəndɪ́ʃən ɪz trúw), swɪ́tʃ-kéjs, fǽn-áwt (wə́n sɔ́rs tə mɛ́nij tɑ́rɡəts) ɔr fǽn-ɪ́n (mɛ́nij sɔ́rsɪz tə wə́n tɑ́rɡət). ɪɡzɛ́kjətərz ɑr ðə prɒ́sɛsɪŋ júwnɪts, íjðər éjdʒənts ɔr kə́stəm fə́ŋkʃənz, ðæt rɪsíjv tájpt mɛ́sɪdʒɪz, dúw wɜ́rk ənd sɛ́nd áwtpʊ̀ts ɔr ɪvɛ́nts. ə WorkflowBuilder ǽssɛmblɪz ɪɡzɛ́kjətərz ənd ɛ́dʒɪz, ənd ðə rə́ntàjm ɪ́ksəkjùwts ðə ɡrǽf ɪn súwpərstɛ̀ps, ə bə́lk sɪ́ŋkrənəs mɒ́dəl ɪn wɪ́tʃ mɛ́sɪdʒɪz ɑr dɪlɪ́vərd ənd prɒ́sɛst ɪn ráwndz. wɜ́rkflòwz ɪmɪ́t ɪvɛ́nts fɔr əbzɜ̀rvəbɪ́lɪtij, səpɔ́rt tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jnts ənd hjúwmən ɪ́npʊ̀t, ənd kən bij dɪfájnd ɪn kówd ɔr dɪklɛ́rətɪvlij ɪn YAML.

Question: A long-running multi-agent workflow must survive process restarts and resume from where it stopped instead of starting over. Which capability should you use?
Explanation: Checkpointing saves the state of a workflow, including executor state, pending messages and pending human-input requests, at the end of supersteps so a run can be resumed or restored later. It lets long-running and human-in-the-loop workflows survive restarts, failures or long waits for approvals, and it supports debugging by replaying from a known point. In Microsoft Agent Framework, you attach checkpoint storage (in memory, file based or durable) to the workflow and resume a run from a checkpoint ID, and pending requests are re-emitted after a restore. For durable execution at scale, agents and workflows can also be hosted with the Durable Task extension for Azure Functions.
trans_Question: ə lɔ́ŋ-rə́nɪŋ mə́ltij-éjdʒənt wɜ́rkflòw məst sərvájv prɒ́sɛs ríjstɑ̀rts ənd rɪzúwm frəm wɛ́r ɪt stɒ́pt ɪnstɛ́d əv stɑ́rtɪŋ ówvər. wɪ́tʃ kèjpəbɪ́lɪtij ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jntɪŋ séjvz ðə stéjt əv ə wɜ́rkflòw, ɪnklúwdɪŋ ɪɡzɛ́kjətər stéjt, pɛ́ndɪŋ mɛ́sɪdʒɪz ənd pɛ́ndɪŋ hjúwmən-ɪ́npʊ̀t rɪkwɛ́sts, ət ðij ɛ́nd əv súwpərstɛ̀ps sów ə rə́n kən bij rɪzúwmd ɔr rɪstɔ́rd léjtər. ɪt lɛ́ts lɔ́ŋ-rə́nɪŋ ənd hjúwmən-ɪn-ðə-lúwp wɜ́rkflòwz sərvájv ríjstɑ̀rts, féjljərz ɔr lɔ́ŋ wéjts fɔr əprúwvəlz, ənd ɪt səpɔ́rts dijbə́ɡɪŋ baj rɛ́plejɪŋ frəm ə nówn pɔ́jnt. ɪn májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk, juw ətǽtʃ tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jnt stɔ́rɪdʒ (ɪn mɛ́mrij, fájl béjst ɔr dʊ́rəbəl) tə ðə wɜ́rkflòw ənd rɪzúwm ə rə́n frəm ə tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jnt ID, ənd pɛ́ndɪŋ rɪkwɛ́sts ɑr rɛ́-ɛ́mɪttɪd ǽftər ə rɪstɔ́r. fɔr dʊ́rəbəl ɪ̀ksəkjúwʃən ət skéjl, éjdʒənts ənd wɜ́rkflòwz kən ɔ́lsow bij hówstɪd wɪð ðə dʊ́rəbəl tǽsk ɪkstɛ́nʃən fɔr ǽʒər fə́ŋkʃənz.

Question: Which open-source SDK from Microsoft is the successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen for building agents and multi-agent workflows in .NET and Python?
Explanation: Microsoft Agent Framework is Microsoft's open-source SDK for building AI agents and multi-agent workflows in .NET and Python, combining the simple agent abstractions of AutoGen with the enterprise features of Semantic Kernel, such as session state, type safety, middleware, telemetry and broad model support. It provides agents with function tools, MCP and A2A support, memory through context providers, graph-based workflows with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop, and built-in orchestrations. Agents built with it can run locally, in your own hosting or as hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service, and DevUI offers a local web interface for testing. Other frameworks, such as LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK, can also be deployed as hosted agents.
trans_Question: wɪ́tʃ ówpən-sɔ́rs SDK frəm májkrəsɔ̀ft ɪz ðə səksɛ́sər tə sɪmǽntɪk kɜ́rnəl ənd ɔ́towdʒɛ̀n fɔr bɪ́ldɪŋ éjdʒənts ənd mə́ltij-éjdʒənt wɜ́rkflòwz ɪn .NET ənd pájθɒn?
trans_Explanation: májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk ɪz májkrəsɔ̀ftz ówpən-sɔ́rs SDK fɔr bɪ́ldɪŋ AI éjdʒənts ənd mə́ltij-éjdʒənt wɜ́rkflòwz ɪn .NET ənd pájθɒn, kəmbájnɪŋ ðə sɪ́mpəl éjdʒənt ǽbstræktɪɒns əv ɔ́towdʒɛ̀n wɪð ðij ɛ́ntərpràjz fíjtʃərz əv sɪmǽntɪk kɜ́rnəl, sə́tʃ æz sɛ́ʃən stéjt, tájp séjftij, mɪ́dəlwɛ̀r, təlɛ́mətrij ənd brɔ́d mɒ́dəl səpɔ́rt. ɪt prəvájdz éjdʒənts wɪð fə́ŋkʃən túwlz, MCP ənd A2A səpɔ́rt, mɛ́mrij θrúw kɒ́ntɛkst prəvájdərz, ɡrǽf-béjst wɜ́rkflòwz wɪð tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jntɪŋ ənd hjúwmən-ɪn-ðə-lúwp, ənd bɪ́lt-ɪn ɔ̀rkɪstréjʃənz. éjdʒənts bɪ́lt wɪð ɪt kən rə́n lówkəlij, ɪn jɔr ówn hówstɪŋ ɔr æz hówstɪd éjdʒənts ɪn fáwndrij éjdʒənt sɜ́rvɪs, ənd DevUI ɔ́fərz ə lówkəl wɛ́b ɪ́ntərfèjs fɔr tɛ́stɪŋ. ə́ðər fréjmwɜ̀rks, sə́tʃ æz lǽŋɡræ̀f ənd ðij ówpənAI éjdʒənts SDK, kən ɔ́lsow bij dɪplɔ́jd æz hówstɪd éjdʒənts.

Question: In Microsoft Agent Framework, a refund function must never run until a human approves each call. How should you define the tool?
Explanation: Function tool approval is a human-in-the-loop control in Microsoft Agent Framework that pauses an agent before a sensitive function runs. In Python you mark the tool with approval_mode set to always_require (never_require skips approval), and in .NET you wrap the function in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction. When the model calls such a tool, the run returns an approval request (user_input_requests in Python, ToolApprovalRequestContent in .NET) with the function name and arguments, and the app resumes the same session with an approve or reject response. Foundry's MCP tool has the equivalent require_approval setting, with mcp_approval_request and mcp_approval_response items.
trans_Question: ɪn májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk, ə rɪfə́nd fə́ŋkʃən məst nɛ́vər rə́n əntɪ́l ə hjúwmən əprúwvz íjtʃ kɔ́l. háw ʃʊd juw dɪfájn ðə túwl?
trans_Explanation: fə́ŋkʃən túwl əprúwvəl ɪz ə hjúwmən-ɪn-ðə-lúwp kəntrówl ɪn májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk ðæt pɔ́zɪz ən éjdʒənt bɪfɔ́r ə sɛ́nsɪtɪv fə́ŋkʃən rə́nz. ɪn pájθɒn juw mɑ́rk ðə túwl wɪð approval_mode sɛ́t tə always_require (never_require skɪ́ps əprúwvəl), ənd ɪn .NET juw rǽp ðə fə́ŋkʃən ɪn ApprovalRequiredAIFunction. wɛ́n ðə mɒ́dəl kɔ́lz sə́tʃ ə túwl, ðə rə́n rɪtɜ́rnz ən əprúwvəl rɪkwɛ́st (user_input_requests ɪn pájθɒn, ToolApprovalRequestContent ɪn .NET) wɪð ðə fə́ŋkʃən néjm ənd ɑ́rɡjəmənts, ənd ðij ǽp rɛ́səmɪz ðə séjm sɛ́ʃən wɪð ən əprúwv ɔr rɪdʒɛ́kt rɪspɒ́ns. fáwndrijz MCP túwl həz ðij ɪkwɪ́vələnt require_approval sɛ́tɪŋ, wɪð mcp_approval_request ənd mcp_approval_response ájtəmz.

Question: In a Microsoft Agent Framework workflow, an executor must pause the workflow and wait for a manager's decision before continuing. Which mechanism should it use?
Explanation: The request and response pattern is how Microsoft Agent Framework workflows obtain human or external input: an executor sends a request (ctx.request_info in Python, a RequestPort in .NET), the workflow pauses and emits a request info event, and the application later sends the response, which the framework routes back to the waiting executor. This enables approvals, clarifying questions and reviews in the middle of a workflow without blocking threads. Pending requests are saved in checkpoints, so a workflow can wait for hours or days and resume after a restart. In agent orchestrations, tool approval requests surface through the same mechanism, and handoff orchestration is interactive by default.
trans_Question: ɪn ə májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk wɜ́rkflòw, ən ɪɡzɛ́kjətər məst pɔ́z ðə wɜ́rkflòw ənd wéjt fɔr ə mǽnɪdʒərz dɪsɪ́ʒən bɪfɔ́r kəntɪ́njuwɪŋ. wɪ́tʃ mɛ́kənɪ̀zəm ʃʊd ɪt júws?
trans_Explanation: ðə rɪkwɛ́st ənd rɪspɒ́ns pǽtərn ɪz háw májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk wɜ́rkflòwz əbtéjn hjúwmən ɔr ɪkstɜ́rnəl ɪ́npʊ̀t: ən ɪɡzɛ́kjətər sɛ́ndz ə rɪkwɛ́st (ctx.request_info ɪn pájθɒn, ə RequestPort ɪn .NET), ðə wɜ́rkflòw pɔ́zɪz ənd ɛ́mɪts ə rɪkwɛ́st ɪ́nfɒ ɪvɛ́nt, ənd ðij æ̀plɪkéjʃən léjtər sɛ́ndz ðə rɪspɒ́ns, wɪ́tʃ ðə fréjmwɜ̀rk rúwts bǽk tə ðə wéjtɪŋ ɪɡzɛ́kjətər. ðɪs ɪnéjbəlz əprúwvəlz, klǽrɪfàjɪŋ kwɛ́stʃənz ənd rɪvjúwz ɪn ðə mɪ́dəl əv ə wɜ́rkflòw wɪðáwt blɒ́kɪŋ θrɛ́dz. pɛ́ndɪŋ rɪkwɛ́sts ɑr séjvd ɪn tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jnts, sów ə wɜ́rkflòw kən wéjt fɔr áwərz ɔr déjz ənd rɪzúwm ǽftər ə rɛ́stært. ɪn éjdʒənt ɔ̀rkɪstréjʃənz, túwl əprúwvəl rɪkwɛ́sts sɜ́rfəs θrúw ðə séjm mɛ́kənɪ̀zəm, ənd hǽndɔ̀f ɔ̀rkɪstréjʃən ɪz ɪ̀ntərǽktɪv baj dɪfɔ́lt.

Question: An autonomous agent sometimes loops, calling tools repeatedly and running up costs without finishing. Which safeguard should you add?
Explanation: A maximum iteration limit is a safeguard that caps how many reasoning and tool-call steps an agent can take in one run, stopping runaway loops and unbounded cost. Autonomous agents act without step-by-step human approval, so they need layered safeguards such as step and time limits, token or cost budgets, tool timeouts, allowlists of permitted actions, confirmations or dry runs for destructive operations, and escalation to a human when confidence is low. Semiautonomous agents add human approval at defined points, which trades speed for control. Monitoring loops, failures and costs in traces lets you tune these limits over time.
trans_Question: ən ɔ̀tɒ́nəməs éjdʒənt sə́mtàjmz lúwps, kɔ́lɪŋ túwlz rɪpíjtɪdlij ənd rə́nɪŋ ə́p kɔ́sts wɪðáwt fɪ́nɪʃɪŋ. wɪ́tʃ séjfɡɑ̀rd ʃʊd juw ǽd?
trans_Explanation: ə mǽksɪməm ɪ̀təréjʃən lɪ́mɪt ɪz ə séjfɡɑ̀rd ðæt kǽps háw mɛ́nij ríjzənɪŋ ənd túwl-kɔ́l stɛ́ps ən éjdʒənt kən téjk ɪn wə́n rə́n, stɒ́pɪŋ rə́nəwèj lúwps ənd ə̀nbáwndɪd kɔ́st. ɔ̀tɒ́nəməs éjdʒənts ǽkt wɪðáwt stɛ́p-baj-stɛ́p hjúwmən əprúwvəl, sów ðej níjd léjərd séjfɡɑ̀rdz sə́tʃ æz stɛ́p ənd tájm lɪ́mɪts, tówkən ɔr kɔ́st bə́dʒəts, túwl tájmàwts, ǽllawlɪsts əv pərmɪ́tɪd ǽkʃənz, kɒ́nfɪrmætɪɒns ɔr dráj rə́nz fɔr dɪstrə́ktɪv ɒ̀pəréjʃənz, ənd ɛ̀skəléjʃən tə ə hjúwmən wɛ́n kɒ́nfɪdəns ɪz lów. sɛ̀mijɔ̀tɒ́nəməs éjdʒənts ǽd hjúwmən əprúwvəl ət dɪfájnd pɔ́jnts, wɪ́tʃ tréjdz spíjd fɔr kəntrówl. mɒ́nɪtərɪŋ lúwps, féjljərz ənd kɔ́sts ɪn tréjsɪz lɛ́ts juw túwn ðijz lɪ́mɪts ówvər tájm.

Question: A workflow step that charges a customer might be retried after a timeout. How should you design the step so that a retry never charges the customer twice?
Explanation: An idempotent action produces the same result no matter how many times it runs, typically by passing a unique idempotency key or request ID that the target system uses to detect and ignore duplicates. Idempotency is essential for agents and workflows because retries after timeouts or transient failures are common, and the caller often can't tell whether the first attempt succeeded. Related reliability patterns include retries with exponential backoff for transient errors, compensating actions (the saga pattern) that undo completed steps when a later step fails, and checkpoints to resume without repeating work. For destructive or financial actions, combine idempotency with human approval and audit logging.
trans_Question: ə wɜ́rkflòw stɛ́p ðæt tʃɑ́rdʒɪz ə kə́stəmər majt bij rijtrájd ǽftər ə tájmàwt. háw ʃʊd juw dɪzájn ðə stɛ́p sów ðət ə rɪtráj nɛ́vər tʃɑ́rdʒɪz ðə kə́stəmər twájs?
trans_Explanation: ən àjdəmpətə́nt ǽkʃən prədúwsɪz ðə séjm rɪzə́lt nów mǽtər háw mɛ́nij tájmz ɪt rə́nz, tɪ́pɪkəlij baj pǽsɪŋ ə juwníjk àjdəmpówtənsij kíj ɔr rɪkwɛ́st ID ðət ðə tɑ́rɡət sɪ́stəm júwzɪz tə dɪtɛ́kt ənd ɪɡnɔ́r djúwplɪkəts. àjdəmpówtənsij ɪz ɪsɛ́nʃəl fɔr éjdʒənts ənd wɜ́rkflòwz bɪkɒ́z rijtrájz ǽftər tájmàwts ɔr trǽnʒənt féjljərz ɑr kɒ́mən, ənd ðə kɔ́lər ɔ́fən kǽnt tɛ́l wɛ́ðər ðə fɜ́rst ətɛ́mpt səksíjdɪd. rɪléjtɪd rɪlàjəbɪ́lɪtij pǽtərnz ɪnklúwd rijtrájz wɪð ɪ̀kspownɛ́nʃəl bǽkɔ̀f fɔr trǽnʒənt ɛ́rərz, kɒ́mpənsèjtɪŋ ǽkʃənz (ðə sǽɡæ pǽtərn) ðæt əndúw kəmplíjtɪd stɛ́ps wɛ́n ə léjtər stɛ́p féjlz, ənd tʃɛ́kpɔ̀jnts tə rɪzúwm wɪðáwt rɪpíjtɪŋ wɜ́rk. fɔr dɪstrə́ktɪv ɔr fájnæ̀nʃəl ǽkʃənz, kɒ́mbajn àjdəmpówtənsij wɪð hjúwmən əprúwvəl ənd ɔ́dɪt lɔ́ɡɪŋ.

Question: A Foundry agent must run automatically every weekday morning to summarize new support tickets, without anyone starting a conversation. What should you configure?
Explanation: A routine in Foundry Agent Service runs an agent automatically when a defined trigger fires, with exactly one trigger and one action that invokes a single prompt agent or hosted agent. Trigger types are timer (run once at a specific time), recurring schedule (cron-style, at least five minutes apart) and event (for example a GitHub issue being opened or a Microsoft Teams message being posted). Routines run with the agent's identity by default, and run history records the inputs, outputs, status and trace of each run. For multistep or branching automation, use workflows instead, or trigger agents from Azure Logic Apps or event-driven code.
trans_Question: ə fáwndrij éjdʒənt məst rə́n ɔ̀təmǽtɪkəlij ɛ́vrij wíjkdèj mɔ́rnɪŋ tə sə́məràjz núw səpɔ́rt tɪ́kəts, wɪðáwt ɛ́nijwə̀n stɑ́rtɪŋ ə kɒ̀nvərséjʃən. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw kənfɪ́ɡjər?
trans_Explanation: ə ruwtíjn ɪn fáwndrij éjdʒənt sɜ́rvɪs rə́nz ən éjdʒənt ɔ̀təmǽtɪkəlij wɛ́n ə dɪfájnd trɪ́ɡər fájərz, wɪð ɪɡzǽktlij wə́n trɪ́ɡər ənd wə́n ǽkʃən ðæt ɪnvówks ə sɪ́ŋɡəl prɒ́mpt éjdʒənt ɔr hówstɪd éjdʒənt. trɪ́ɡər tájps ɑr tɪ́mɛr (rə́n wə́ns ət ə spɪsɪ́fɪk tájm), rɪkɜ́rɪŋ skɛ́dʒuwl (krɒ́n-stájl, ət líjst fájv mɪ́nəts əpɑ́rt) ənd ɪvɛ́nt (fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl ə ɡɪ́thə̀b ɪ́ʃuw bíjɪŋ ówpənd ɔr ə májkrəsɔ̀ft tíjmz mɛ́sɪdʒ bíjɪŋ pówstɪd). ruwtíjnz rə́n wɪð ðij éjdʒənts ajdɛ́ntɪtij baj dɪfɔ́lt, ənd rə́n hɪ́strij rɛ́kərdz ðij ɪ́npʊ̀ts, áwtpʊ̀ts, stéjtəs ənd tréjs əv íjtʃ rə́n. fɔr mə́ltijstɛp ɔr brǽntʃɪŋ ɔtəméjʃən, júws wɜ́rkflòwz ɪnstɛ́d, ɔr trɪ́ɡər éjdʒənts frəm ǽʒər lɒ́dʒɪk ǽps ɔr ɪvɛ́nt-drɪ́vən kówd.

Question: An agent sometimes offers discounts that its system message forbids. Which evaluator detects an agent breaking its assigned rules and policies?
Explanation: The Task Adherence evaluator (preview) is an agent evaluator that checks whether an agent's actions and responses follow its assigned task, rules, procedures and policy constraints, based on its system message and prior steps, and returns pass or fail. Agent evaluators are grouped into system evaluators, which judge end-to-end outcomes (Task Completion, Task Adherence, Intent Resolution, Customer Satisfaction and Task Navigation Efficiency), and process evaluators, which judge individual steps and tool calls (Tool Call Accuracy, Tool Selection, Tool Input Accuracy, Tool Output Utilization and Tool Call Success). They accept a query and response or a full messages list, and many also use tool_definitions. Composite evaluators such as Output Quality and Tool Use Quality (preview) batch several checks into one judge call.
trans_Question: ən éjdʒənt sə́mtàjmz ɔ́fərz dɪ́skàwnts ðæt ɪts sɪ́stəm mɛ́sɪdʒ fərbɪ́dz. wɪ́tʃ ɪvǽljuwèjtər dɪtɛ́kts ən éjdʒənt bréjkɪŋ ɪts əsájnd rúwlz ənd pɒ́lɪsijz?
trans_Explanation: ðə tǽsk ədhɪ́rəns ɪvǽljuwèjtər (príjvjuw) ɪz ən éjdʒənt ɪvǽljuwèjtər ðæt tʃɛ́ks wɛ́ðər ən éjdʒənts ǽkʃənz ənd rɪspɒ́nsɪz fɒ́low ɪts əsájnd tǽsk, rúwlz, prəsíjdʒərz ənd pɒ́lɪsij kənstréjnts, béjst ɒn ɪts sɪ́stəm mɛ́sɪdʒ ənd prájər stɛ́ps, ənd rɪtɜ́rnz pǽs ɔr féjl. éjdʒənt ɪvǽljuwèjtərz ɑr ɡrúwpt ɪ́ntə sɪ́stəm ɪvǽljuwèjtərz, wɪ́tʃ dʒə́dʒ ɛ́nd-tə-ɛ́nd áwtkə̀mz (tǽsk kəmplíjʃən, tǽsk ədhɪ́rəns, ɪntɛ́nt rɛ̀zəlúwʃən, kə́stəmər sæ̀tɪsfǽkʃən ənd tǽsk næ̀vɪɡéjʃən ɪfɪ́ʃənsij), ənd prɒ́sɛs ɪvǽljuwèjtərz, wɪ́tʃ dʒə́dʒ ɪ̀ndɪvɪ́dʒuwəl stɛ́ps ənd túwl kɔ́lz (túwl kɔ́l ǽkjərəsij, túwl sɪlɛ́kʃən, túwl ɪ́npʊ̀t ǽkjərəsij, túwl áwtpʊ̀t juwtəlɪzéjʃən ənd túwl kɔ́l səksɛ́s). ðej əksɛ́pt ə kwíjrij ənd rɪspɒ́ns ɔr ə fʊ́l mɛ́sɪdʒɪz lɪ́st, ənd mɛ́nij ɔ́lsow júws tool_definitions. kɒ́mpɒsɪt ɪvǽljuwèjtərz sə́tʃ æz áwtpʊ̀t kwɑ́lɪtij ənd túwl júws kwɑ́lɪtij (príjvjuw) bǽtʃ sɛ́vrəl tʃɛ́ks ɪ́ntə wə́n dʒə́dʒ kɔ́l.

Question: You need to measure whether an agent correctly understands what each user is actually asking for. Which evaluator should you use?
Explanation: The Intent Resolution evaluator (preview) is an agent evaluator that measures whether an agent correctly identifies the user's intent and addresses it, scoring on a 1 to 5 scale with a pass or fail threshold. Misunderstood intent is a common root cause of agent failures, such as calling the wrong tool or answering a different question. The Task Completion evaluator (preview) complements it by checking whether the agent delivered a usable result that meets all user requirements, and Customer Satisfaction (preview) estimates satisfaction across helpfulness, completeness, clarity, tone, resolution and adaptability. These system evaluators judge outcomes, while process evaluators inspect individual tool calls.

trans_Explanation: ðij ɪntɛ́nt rɛ̀zəlúwʃən ɪvǽljuwèjtər (príjvjuw) ɪz ən éjdʒənt ɪvǽljuwèjtər ðæt mɛ́ʒərz wɛ́ðər ən éjdʒənt kərɛ́ktlij ajdɛ́ntɪfàjz ðə júwzərz ɪntɛ́nt ənd ədrɛ́sɪz ɪt, skɔ́rɪŋ ɒn ə 1 tə 5 skéjl wɪð ə pǽs ɔr féjl θrɛ́ʃòwld. mɪ̀sə̀ndərstʊ́d ɪntɛ́nt ɪz ə kɒ́mən rúwt kɔ́z əv éjdʒənt féjljərz, sə́tʃ æz kɔ́lɪŋ ðə rɔ́ŋ túwl ɔr ǽnsərɪŋ ə dɪ́frənt kwɛ́stʃən. ðə tǽsk kəmplíjʃən ɪvǽljuwèjtər (príjvjuw) kɒ́mpləmənts ɪt baj tʃɛ́kɪŋ wɛ́ðər ðij éjdʒənt dɪlɪ́vərd ə júwzəbəl rɪzə́lt ðæt míjts ɔ́l júwzər rɪkwájərmənts, ənd kə́stəmər sæ̀tɪsfǽkʃən (príjvjuw) ɛ́stɪməts sæ̀tɪsfǽkʃən əkrɔ́s hɛ́lpfəlnəs, kəmplíjtnəs, klǽrɪtij, tówn, rɛ̀zəlúwʃən ənd ədæ̀ptəbɪ́lɪtij. ðijz sɪ́stəm ɪvǽljuwèjtərz dʒə́dʒ áwtkə̀mz, wájl prɒ́sɛs ɪvǽljuwèjtərz ɪ̀nspɛ́kt ɪ̀ndɪvɪ́dʒuwəl túwl kɔ́lz.

Question: You need to evaluate whether an agent made the right tool calls with correct parameters to complete its tasks. Which evaluator should you use?
Explanation: The Tool Call Accuracy evaluator is an agent process evaluator that judges whether an agent made the right tool calls, with correct parameters, to complete its task, scoring on a 1 to 5 scale with a pass or fail threshold. It needs the query and the tool_definitions, plus the tool calls or the full messages. Finer-grained process evaluators include Tool Selection (right tools, no unnecessary ones), Tool Input Accuracy (parameters grounded, correctly typed and formatted, none missing or unexpected) and Tool Output Utilization (tool results used correctly in the response). Several tool evaluators have limited support for conversations that call built-in tools such as Azure AI Search, Bing grounding, web search or code interpreter.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə ɪvǽljuwèjt wɛ́ðər ən éjdʒənt méjd ðə rájt túwl kɔ́lz wɪð kərɛ́kt pərǽmətərz tə kəmplíjt ɪts tǽsks. wɪ́tʃ ɪvǽljuwèjtər ʃʊd juw júws?

Question: Some agent tool calls fail with timeouts, HTTP errors or exceptions. Which evaluator measures this?
Explanation: The Tool Call Success evaluator is an agent process evaluator that checks whether tool calls succeeded or resulted in technical errors or exceptions, such as timeouts, HTTP errors or failed executions, and returns pass or fail. It needs only the response or messages that contain the tool calls and their outputs. Technical failures differ from logical errors, such as choosing the wrong tool (Tool Selection) or passing wrong arguments (Tool Input Accuracy), so evaluating both helps locate the root cause. Tool failures in production also appear in traces as failed spans, which you can correlate with the run success rate on the monitoring dashboard.
trans_Question: səm éjdʒənt túwl kɔ́lz féjl wɪð tájmàwts, HTTP ɛ́rərz ɔr ɪksɛ́pʃənz. wɪ́tʃ ɪvǽljuwèjtər mɛ́ʒərz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: ðə túwl kɔ́l səksɛ́s ɪvǽljuwèjtər ɪz ən éjdʒənt prɒ́sɛs ɪvǽljuwèjtər ðæt tʃɛ́ks wɛ́ðər túwl kɔ́lz səksíjdɪd ɔr rɪzə́ltɪd ɪn tɛ́knɪkəl ɛ́rərz ɔr ɪksɛ́pʃənz, sə́tʃ æz tájmàwts, HTTP ɛ́rərz ɔr féjld ɛ̀ksɪkjúwʃənz, ənd rɪtɜ́rnz pǽs ɔr féjl. ɪt níjdz ównlij ðə rɪspɒ́ns ɔr mɛ́sɪdʒɪz ðæt kəntéjn ðə túwl kɔ́lz ənd ðɛr áwtpʊ̀ts. tɛ́knɪkəl féjljərz dɪ́fər frəm lɒ́dʒɪkəl ɛ́rərz, sə́tʃ æz tʃúwzɪŋ ðə rɔ́ŋ túwl (túwl sɪlɛ́kʃən) ɔr pǽsɪŋ rɔ́ŋ ɑ́rɡjəmənts (túwl ɪ́npʊ̀t ǽkjərəsij), sów ɪvǽljuwèjtɪŋ bówθ hɛ́lps lówkèjt ðə rúwt kɔ́z. túwl féjljərz ɪn prədə́kʃən ɔ́lsow əpɪ́r ɪn tréjsɪz æz féjld spǽnz, wɪ́tʃ juw kən kɔ́rəlèjt wɪð ðə rə́n səksɛ́s réjt ɒn ðə mɒ́nɪtərɪŋ dǽʃbɔ̀rd.

Question: You have the expected sequence of tool calls for each test task and want precision and recall scores for how closely the agent's actual calls match it. Which evaluator should you use?
Explanation: The Task Navigation Efficiency evaluator is an agent system evaluator that compares an agent's actual tool calls with an expected sequence (expected_actions, which act as ground truth) to determine whether the agent reached its goal efficiently, without unnecessary or missing steps. It returns pass or fail together with precision, recall and F1 scores, and a matching mode controls how strictly order and extra steps are treated. It is well suited to regression tests of agent workflows whose correct path is known. Inefficient paths increase latency and cost even when the final answer is correct.

Question: Which Foundry feature shows token usage, latency, run success rate, evaluation scores and red teaming results for a deployed agent over time?
Explanation: The Agent Monitoring Dashboard in the Foundry portal shows operational and quality metrics for deployed agents: token usage, latency, run success rate, evaluation metrics from evaluators that run on sampled outputs, and results of scheduled red team scans. It reads telemetry from the Application Insights resource connected to the project, so connecting Application Insights is a prerequisite. Its settings let you configure continuous evaluation of live traffic (limited to 100 runs per hour by default), recurring evaluations, scheduled red team scans and alerts on latency, token usage, evaluation scores or red team findings. Use it to spot regressions, then drill into traces to find the root cause.
trans_Question: wɪ́tʃ fáwndrij fíjtʃər ʃówz tówkən júwsɪdʒ, léjtənsij, rə́n səksɛ́s réjt, ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən skɔ́rz ənd rɛ́d tíjmɪŋ rɪzə́lts fɔr ə dɪplɔ́jd éjdʒənt ówvər tájm?
trans_Explanation: ðij éjdʒənt mɒ́nɪtərɪŋ dǽʃbɔ̀rd ɪn ðə fáwndrij pɔ́rtəl ʃówz ɒ̀pəréjʃənəl ənd kwɑ́lɪtij mɛ́trɪks fɔr dɪplɔ́jd éjdʒənts: tówkən júwsɪdʒ, léjtənsij, rə́n səksɛ́s réjt, ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən mɛ́trɪks frəm ɪvǽljuwèjtərz ðæt rə́n ɒn sǽmpəld áwtpʊ̀ts, ənd rɪzə́lts əv skɛ́dʒuwld rɛ́d tíjm skǽnz. ɪt ríjdz təlɛ́mətrij frəm ðij æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts ríjsɔrs kənɛ́ktɪd tə ðə prɒ́dʒɛkt, sów kənɛ́ktɪŋ æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts ɪz ə prɛ́rɛkwɪsɪt. ɪts sɛ́tɪŋz lɛ́t juw kənfɪ́ɡjər kəntɪ́njuwəs ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən əv lɪ́v trǽfɪk (lɪ́mɪtɪd tə 100 rə́nz pə́r áwər baj dɪfɔ́lt), rɪkɜ́rɪŋ ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃənz, skɛ́dʒuwld rɛ́d tíjm skǽnz ənd əlɜ́rts ɒn léjtənsij, tówkən júwsɪdʒ, ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən skɔ́rz ɔr rɛ́d tíjm fájndɪŋz. júws ɪt tə spɒ́t rɪɡrɛ́ʃənz, ðɛ́n drɪ́l ɪ́ntə tréjsɪz tə fájnd ðə rúwt kɔ́z.

Question: After an evaluation run, you need to group hundreds of failing samples into common failure patterns with suggested fixes. Which Foundry feature should you use?
Explanation: Evaluation cluster analysis (preview) is a Foundry error analysis feature that groups samples from one or more evaluation runs by semantic similarity, using embedding-based clustering of outputs and evaluator feedback, so you can see recurring failure types and how often each occurs. Each cluster has an auto-generated description of the likely cause and recommendations, and you can drill into subclusters and individual samples with their scores, conversations and trace IDs. The analysis needs a deployed model and isn't stored, so download it as CSV to keep it. Typical follow-ups are refining instructions, adjusting tools or curating fine-tuning data, then re-running the evaluation to confirm the fix.

Question: A model's output format varies between requests. You add three example inputs with their ideal outputs to the prompt. Which technique is this?
Explanation: Few-shot prompting is a prompt engineering technique that includes a small number of example input and output pairs in the prompt so the model infers the expected pattern, format, tone or labeling scheme, while zero-shot prompting gives only instructions and one-shot gives a single example. Examples are powerful for consistent formatting and classification, but they add tokens to every request and can bias outputs toward the examples, so keep them diverse and representative. Other core techniques include clear instructions with explicit output formats, delimiters such as Markdown sections or XML tags to separate instructions from content, role or persona prompting and grounding instructions that tell the model to answer only from provided sources. Reasoning models often need fewer or no examples, and too many examples can reduce their performance.
trans_Question: ə mɒ́dəlz áwtpʊ̀t fɔ́rmæ̀t vɛ́rijz bɪtwíjn rɪkwɛ́sts. juw ǽd θríj ɪɡzǽmpəl ɪ́npʊ̀ts wɪð ðɛr ajdíjəl áwtpʊ̀ts tə ðə prɒ́mpt. wɪ́tʃ tɛkníjk ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: fjúw-ʃɒ́t prɒ́mptɪŋ ɪz ə prɒ́mpt ɛ̀ndʒɪnɪ́rɪŋ tɛkníjk ðæt ɪnklúwdz ə smɔ́l nə́mbər əv ɪɡzǽmpəl ɪ́npʊ̀t ənd áwtpʊ̀t pɛ́rz ɪn ðə prɒ́mpt sów ðə mɒ́dəl ɪ́nfɛrs ðij ɪkspɛ́ktɪd pǽtərn, fɔ́rmæ̀t, tówn ɔr léjblɪŋ skíjm, wájl zɪ́row-ʃɒ́t prɒ́mptɪŋ ɡɪ́vz ównlij ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz ənd wə́n-ʃɒ́t ɡɪ́vz ə sɪ́ŋɡəl ɪɡzǽmpəl. ɪɡzǽmpəlz ɑr páwərfəl fɔr kənsɪ́stənt fɔ́rmæ̀tɪŋ ənd klæ̀sɪfɪkéjʃən, bət ðej ǽd tówkənz tə ɛ́vrij rɪkwɛ́st ənd kən bájəs áwtpʊ̀ts təwɔ́rd ðij ɪɡzǽmpəlz, sów kíjp ðɛm dɪvɜ́rs ənd rɛ̀prɪzɛ́ntətɪv. ə́ðər kɔ́r tɛkníjks ɪnklúwd klɪ́r ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz wɪð ɪksplɪ́sɪt áwtpʊ̀t fɔ́rmæ̀ts, dɪlɪ́mɪtərz sə́tʃ æz mɑ́rkdàwn sɛ́kʃənz ɔr XML tǽɡz tə sɛ́prət ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz frəm kɒ́ntɛnt, rówl ɔr pərsównə prɒ́mptɪŋ ənd ɡráwndɪŋ ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz ðæt tɛ́l ðə mɒ́dəl tə ǽnsər ównlij frəm prəvájdɪd sɔ́rsɪz. ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz ɔ́fən níjd fjúwər ɔr nów ɪɡzǽmpəlz, ənd túw mɛ́nij ɪɡzǽmpəlz kən rɪdúws ðɛr pərfɔ́rməns.

Question: A ticket classification app gives different labels for the same ticket on repeated calls. Which parameter change makes outputs more consistent?
Explanation: Temperature is a sampling parameter, ranging from 0 to 2 with a default of 1, that controls randomness: low values make the model pick the most likely tokens for focused, more repeatable outputs, and high values make outputs more varied and creative. top_p (nucleus sampling, 0 to 1) is an alternative that limits sampling to the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p, and the usual guidance is to adjust temperature or top_p, not both. Even at temperature 0 outputs aren't guaranteed to be identical, and the seed parameter only gives best-effort reproducibility. Reasoning models don't support temperature, top_p, presence or frequency penalties, logprobs or logit_bias, so you steer them with instructions, reasoning effort and verbosity instead.
trans_Question: ə tɪ́kət klæ̀sɪfɪkéjʃən ǽp ɡɪ́vz dɪ́frənt léjbəlz fɔr ðə séjm tɪ́kət ɒn rɪpíjtɪd kɔ́lz. wɪ́tʃ pərǽmətər tʃéjndʒ méjks áwtpʊ̀ts mɔ́r kənsɪ́stənt?
trans_Explanation: tɛ́mprətʃər ɪz ə sǽmplɪŋ pərǽmətər, réjndʒɪŋ frəm 0 tə 2 wɪð ə dɪfɔ́lt əv 1, ðæt kəntrówlz rǽndəmnəs: lów vǽljuwz méjk ðə mɒ́dəl pɪ́k ðə mówst lájklij tówkənz fɔr fówkəst, mɔ́r rɪpíjtəbəl áwtpʊ̀ts, ənd háj vǽljuwz méjk áwtpʊ̀ts mɔ́r vɛ́rijd ənd krijéjtɪv. top_p (núwklijəs sǽmplɪŋ, 0 tə 1) ɪz ən ɔltɜ́rnətɪv ðæt lɪ́mɪts sǽmplɪŋ tə ðə smɔ́ləst sɛ́t əv tówkənz húwz kjúwmjələtɪv prɒ̀bəbɪ́lɪtij ríjtʃɪz p, ənd ðə júwʒəwəl ɡájdəns ɪz tə ədʒə́st tɛ́mprətʃər ɔr top_p, nɒ́t bówθ. íjvən ət tɛ́mprətʃər 0 áwtpʊ̀ts ɑ́rnt ɡæ̀rəntíjd tə bij ajdɛ́ntɪkəl, ənd ðə síjd pərǽmətər ównlij ɡɪ́vz bɛ́st-ɛ́fərt rìjprədùwsɪbɪ́lɪtij. ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz dównt səpɔ́rt tɛ́mprətʃər, top_p, prɛ́zəns ɔr fríjkwənsij pɛ́nəltijz, lɒ́ɡprɒbs ɔr logit_bias, sów juw stɪ́r ðɛm wɪð ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz, ríjzənɪŋ ɛ́fərt ənd vərbɒ́sətij ɪnstɛ́d.

Question: You need the model to stop generating as soon as it outputs the marker ###. Which parameter should you use?
Explanation: A stop sequence is a string (up to four in the Chat Completions API) that makes the model stop generating as soon as it would produce that text, and the stop sequence itself isn't included in the output. Stop sequences are useful for ending a list, a section or a single record cleanly, and for preventing the model from continuing into an imagined next turn. Other output controls include max_output_tokens or max_completion_tokens (a hard length cap), logit_bias (raising or lowering the likelihood of specific token IDs, from -100 to 100), n (several choices per request) and logprobs (token probabilities for confidence analysis). Structured outputs with a JSON Schema are usually more reliable than stop sequences for producing machine-readable formats.
trans_Question: juw níjd ðə mɒ́dəl tə stɒ́p dʒɛ́nərèjtɪŋ æz súwn æz ɪt áwtpʊ̀ts ðə mǽrkɛr ###. wɪ́tʃ pərǽmətər ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: ə stɒ́p síjkwəns ɪz ə strɪ́ŋ (ə́p tə fɔ́r ɪn ðə tʃǽt kəmplíjʃənz API) ðæt méjks ðə mɒ́dəl stɒ́p dʒɛ́nərèjtɪŋ æz súwn æz ɪt wʊd prədúws ðæt tɛ́kst, ənd ðə stɒ́p síjkwəns ɪtsɛ́lf ɪ́zənt ɪnklúwdɪd ɪn ðij áwtpʊ̀t. stɒ́p síjkwənsɪz ɑr júwsfəl fɔr ɛ́ndɪŋ ə lɪ́st, ə sɛ́kʃən ɔr ə sɪ́ŋɡəl rɛ́kərd klíjnlij, ənd fɔr prɪvɛ́ntɪŋ ðə mɒ́dəl frəm kəntɪ́njuwɪŋ ɪ́ntə ən ɪmǽdʒɪnd nɛ́kst tɜ́rn. ə́ðər áwtpʊ̀t kəntrówlz ɪnklúwd max_output_tokens ɔr max_completion_tokens (ə hɑ́rd lɛ́ŋθ kǽp), logit_bias (réjzɪŋ ɔr lówərɪŋ ðə lájklijhʊ̀d əv spɪsɪ́fɪk tówkən IDz, frəm -100 tə 100), n (sɛ́vrəl tʃɔ́jsɪz pə́r rɪkwɛ́st) ənd lɒ́ɡprɒbs (tówkən prɒ̀bəbɪ́lɪtijz fɔr kɒ́nfɪdəns ənǽlɪsɪs). strə́ktʃərd áwtpʊ̀ts wɪð ə JSON skíjmə ɑr júwʒəwəlij mɔ́r rɪlájəbəl ðən stɒ́p síjkwənsɪz fɔr prədúwsɪŋ məʃíjn-ríjdəbəl fɔ́rmæ̀ts.

Question: Generated product descriptions repeat the same phrases word for word many times. Which parameter should you increase?
Explanation: The frequency_penalty parameter, ranging from -2.0 to 2.0 with a default of 0, penalizes tokens in proportion to how often they have already appeared in the text, which reduces verbatim repetition. The related presence_penalty applies a one-time penalty to any token that has appeared at all, which encourages the model to move to new topics rather than reducing repetition of frequent words. Positive values discourage repetition and negative values encourage it, and very high values can make text incoherent, so small adjustments such as 0.5 work best. Neither penalty is supported by reasoning models.
trans_Question: dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd prɒ́dəkt dɪskrɪ́pʃənz rɪpíjt ðə séjm fréjzɪz wɜ́rd fɔr wɜ́rd mɛ́nij tájmz. wɪ́tʃ pərǽmətər ʃʊd juw ɪ́nkrìjs?
trans_Explanation: ðə frequency_penalty pərǽmətər, réjndʒɪŋ frəm -2.0 tə 2.0 wɪð ə dɪfɔ́lt əv 0, pɛ́nælɪzɪz tówkənz ɪn prəpɔ́rʃən tə háw ɔ́fən ðej həv ɔlrɛ́dij əpɪ́rd ɪn ðə tɛ́kst, wɪ́tʃ rɪdúwsɪz vərbéjtɪm rɛ̀pətɪ́ʃən. ðə rɪléjtɪd presence_penalty əplájz ə wə́n-tájm pɛ́nəltij tə ɛ́nij tówkən ðǽt həz əpɪ́rd ət ɔ́l, wɪ́tʃ ɪnkɜ́rɪdʒɪz ðə mɒ́dəl tə múwv tə núw tɒ́pɪks rǽðər ðən rɪdúwsɪŋ rɛ̀pətɪ́ʃən əv fríjkwənt wɜ́rdz. pɒ́zɪtɪv vǽljuwz dɪskɜ́rɪdʒ rɛ̀pətɪ́ʃən ənd nɛ́ɡətɪv vǽljuwz ɪnkɜ́rɪdʒ ɪt, ənd vɛ́rij háj vǽljuwz kən méjk tɛ́kst ɪ́nkɒhɛrɛnt, sów smɔ́l ədʒə́stmənts sə́tʃ æz 0.5 wɜ́rk bɛ́st. níjðər pɛ́nəltij ɪz səpɔ́rtɪd baj ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz.

Question: A reasoning model is slow and expensive on simple lookups that don't need deep thinking. Which setting should you change?
Explanation: Reasoning effort (reasoning.effort in the Responses API, reasoning_effort in Chat Completions) controls how many internal reasoning tokens a reasoning model spends before answering, with values such as low, medium and high, and some newer models add minimal or none for the fastest responses. Lower effort reduces latency and cost for simple tasks, and higher effort improves accuracy on complex multistep problems. Reasoning tokens are hidden but billed as output tokens and count toward max_completion_tokens or max_output_tokens, so set those limits high enough to avoid incomplete responses. The Responses API can return a reasoning summary, and GPT-5 series models also accept a verbosity parameter that controls how long the final answer is.
trans_Question: ə ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəl ɪz slów ənd ɪkspɛ́nsɪv ɒn sɪ́mpəl lúwkəps ðæt dównt níjd díjp θɪ́ŋkɪŋ. wɪ́tʃ sɛ́tɪŋ ʃʊd juw tʃéjndʒ?
trans_Explanation: ríjzənɪŋ ɛ́fərt (reasoning.effort ɪn ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API, reasoning_effort ɪn tʃǽt kəmplíjʃənz) kəntrówlz háw mɛ́nij ɪntɜ́rnəl ríjzənɪŋ tówkənz ə ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəl spɛ́ndz bɪfɔ́r ǽnsərɪŋ, wɪð vǽljuwz sə́tʃ æz lów, míjdijəm ənd háj, ənd səm núwər mɒ́dəlz ǽd mɪ́nɪməl ɔr nə́n fɔr ðə fǽstəst rɪspɒ́nsɪz. lówər ɛ́fərt rɪdúwsɪz léjtənsij ənd kɔ́st fɔr sɪ́mpəl tǽsks, ənd hájər ɛ́fərt ɪ̀mprúwvz ǽkjərəsij ɒn kəmplɛ́ks mə́ltijstɛp prɒ́bləmz. ríjzənɪŋ tówkənz ɑr hɪ́dən bət bɪ́ld æz áwtpʊ̀t tówkənz ənd káwnt təwɔ́rd max_completion_tokens ɔr max_output_tokens, sów sɛ́t ðowz lɪ́mɪts háj ɪnə́f tə əvɔ́jd ɪ̀nkəmplíjt rɪspɒ́nsɪz. ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API kən rɪtɜ́rn ə ríjzənɪŋ sə́mərij, ənd GPT-5 sɪ́rijz mɒ́dəlz ɔ́lsow əksɛ́pt ə vərbɒ́sətij pərǽmətər ðæt kəntrówlz háw lɔ́ŋ ðə fájnəl ǽnsər ɪz.

Question: Responses are cut off mid-sentence and the API reports a finish_reason of length. What should you change?
Explanation: The output token limit caps how many tokens a model can generate in one response: max_output_tokens in the Responses API, max_completion_tokens in Chat Completions (which also covers reasoning tokens), and the legacy max_tokens, which reasoning models don't support. When the limit is reached, Chat Completions returns finish_reason length and the Responses API returns status incomplete with the reason max_output_tokens, so the output is truncated. For reasoning models, hidden reasoning tokens consume the same budget, so a low limit can produce an empty or partial answer. The input plus output must also fit the model's context window, and other finish reasons include stop (natural end), tool_calls and content_filter.
trans_Question: rɪspɒ́nsɪz ɑr kə́t ɔ́f mɪ́d-sɛ́ntəns ənd ðə API rɪpɔ́rts ə finish_reason əv lɛ́ŋθ. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw tʃéjndʒ?
trans_Explanation: ðij áwtpʊ̀t tówkən lɪ́mɪt kǽps háw mɛ́nij tówkənz ə mɒ́dəl kən dʒɛ́nərèjt ɪn wə́n rɪspɒ́ns: max_output_tokens ɪn ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API, max_completion_tokens ɪn tʃǽt kəmplíjʃənz (wɪ́tʃ ɔ́lsow kə́vərz ríjzənɪŋ tówkənz), ənd ðə lɛ́ɡəsij max_tokens, wɪ́tʃ ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz dównt səpɔ́rt. wɛ́n ðə lɪ́mɪt ɪz ríjtʃt, tʃǽt kəmplíjʃənz rɪtɜ́rnz finish_reason lɛ́ŋθ ənd ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API rɪtɜ́rnz stéjtəs ɪ̀nkəmplíjt wɪð ðə ríjzən max_output_tokens, sów ðij áwtpʊ̀t ɪz trə́ŋkèjtɪd. fɔr ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz, hɪ́dən ríjzənɪŋ tówkənz kənsúwm ðə séjm bə́dʒət, sów ə lów lɪ́mɪt kən prədúws ən ɛ́mptij ɔr pɑ́rʃəl ǽnsər. ðij ɪ́npʊ̀t plə́s áwtpʊ̀t məst ɔ́lsow fɪ́t ðə mɒ́dəlz kɒ́ntɛkst wɪ́ndow, ənd ə́ðər fɪ́nɪʃ ríjzənz ɪnklúwd stɒ́p (nǽtʃərəl ɛ́nd), tool_calls ənd content_filter.

Question: Prompt engineering with examples hasn't made a model reliably follow your company's complex output style across thousands of requests. Knowledge isn't the problem. What should you try next?
Explanation: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) further trains a base model on example conversations (JSONL training and validation files in the chat messages format) so it learns a desired behavior, style, format or task, which can also shorten prompts and cut latency and cost. The usual optimization order is prompt engineering first, RAG when the model lacks knowledge or needs current or private data, and fine-tuning when behavior, consistency or format must improve beyond what prompts achieve. Azure OpenAI fine-tuning uses LoRA (low-rank adaptation), needs at least 10 examples (with 50 or more well-crafted examples as a common starting point), exposes hyperparameters such as epochs, batch size and learning rate multiplier, and offers Standard, Global and Developer training types. The resulting fine-tuned model must be deployed before use, and deployments are billed for hosting as well as tokens.
trans_Question: prɒ́mpt ɛ̀ndʒɪnɪ́rɪŋ wɪð ɪɡzǽmpəlz hǽsnt méjd ə mɒ́dəl rɪlájəblij fɒ́low jɔr kə́mpənijz kəmplɛ́ks áwtpʊ̀t stájl əkrɔ́s θáwzəndz əv rɪkwɛ́sts. nɒ́lɪdʒ ɪ́zənt ðə prɒ́bləm. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw tráj nɛ́kst?
trans_Explanation: súwpərvàjzd fájn-túwnɪŋ (SFT) fɜ́rðər tréjnz ə béjs mɒ́dəl ɒn ɪɡzǽmpəl kɒ̀nvərséjʃənz (JSONL tréjnɪŋ ənd væ̀lɪdéjʃən fájlz ɪn ðə tʃǽt mɛ́sɪdʒɪz fɔ́rmæ̀t) sów ɪt lɜ́rnz ə dɪzájərd bɪhéjvjərz, stájl, fɔ́rmæ̀t ɔr tǽsk, wɪ́tʃ kən ɔ́lsow ʃɔ́rtən prɒ́mpts ənd kə́t léjtənsij ənd kɔ́st. ðə júwʒəwəl ɒ̀ptɪmɪzéjʃən ɔ́rdər ɪz prɒ́mpt ɛ̀ndʒɪnɪ́rɪŋ fɜ́rst, RAG wɛ́n ðə mɒ́dəl lǽks nɒ́lɪdʒ ɔr níjdz kɜ́rənt ɔr prájvət déjtə, ənd fájn-túwnɪŋ wɛ́n bɪhéjvjərz, kənsɪ́stənsij ɔr fɔ́rmæ̀t məst ɪmprúwv bɪjɒ́nd wɒ́t prɒ́mpts ətʃíjv. ǽʒər ówpənAI fájn-túwnɪŋ júwzɪz lówrɑ (lów-rǽŋk æ̀dəptéjʃən), níjdz ət líjst 10 ɪɡzǽmpəlz (wɪð 50 ɔr mɔ́r wɛ́l-krǽftɪd ɪɡzǽmpəlz æz ə kɒ́mən stɑ́rtɪŋ pɔ́jnt), ɪkspówzɪz hjpɛ́rpæræmɛtɛrs sə́tʃ æz ɛ́pɒtʃs, bǽtʃ sájz ənd lɜ́rnɪŋ réjt mə́ltɪplɪɛr, ənd ɔ́fərz stǽndərd, ɡlówbəl ənd dɪvɛ́ləpər tréjnɪŋ tájps. ðə rɪzə́ltɪŋ fájn-túwnd mɒ́dəl məst bij dɪplɔ́jd bɪfɔ́r júws, ənd dɪplɔ́jmənts ɑr bɪ́ld fɔr hówstɪŋ æz wɛ́l æz tówkənz.

Question: You have pairs of preferred and non-preferred responses for the same prompts and want to align a model's tone and judgment with the preferred ones. Which fine-tuning method fits?
Explanation: Direct preference optimization (DPO) is a fine-tuning method that adjusts model weights using pairs of responses to the same input, one preferred and one non-preferred, so the model learns subjective qualities such as tone, style, helpfulness or safety from human preferences. Its training data contains the input messages, a preferred_output and a non_preferred_output, and it is computationally lighter than reinforcement learning from human feedback because it needs no separate reward model. Supervised fine-tuning instead learns from single ideal responses, and DPO is often applied after SFT. Reinforcement fine-tuning uses a grader to reward correct reasoning on tasks with verifiable answers.
trans_Question: juw həv pɛ́rz əv prɪfɜ́rd ənd nɒ́n-prɪfɜ́rd rɪspɒ́nsɪz fɔr ðə séjm prɒ́mpts ənd wɒ́nt tə əlájn ə mɒ́dəlz tówn ənd dʒə́dʒmənt wɪð ðə prɪfɜ́rd wə́nz. wɪ́tʃ fájn-túwnɪŋ mɛ́θəd fɪ́ts?
trans_Explanation: dɪrɛ́kt prɛ́frəns ɒ̀ptɪmɪzéjʃən (DPO) ɪz ə fájn-túwnɪŋ mɛ́θəd ðæt ədʒə́sts mɒ́dəl wéjts júwzɪŋ pɛ́rz əv rɪspɒ́nsɪz tə ðə séjm ɪ́npʊ̀t, wə́n prɪfɜ́rd ənd wə́n nɒ́n-prɪfɜ́rd, sów ðə mɒ́dəl lɜ́rnz səbdʒɛ́ktɪv kwɑ́lɪtijz sə́tʃ æz tówn, stájl, hɛ́lpfəlnəs ɔr séjftij frəm hjúwmən prɛ́frənsɪz. ɪts tréjnɪŋ déjtə kəntéjnz ðij ɪ́npʊ̀t mɛ́sɪdʒɪz, ə preferred_output ənd ə non_preferred_output, ənd ɪt ɪz kɒ́mpətætɪɒnællij lájtər ðən rìjɪnfɔ́rsmənt lɜ́rnɪŋ frəm hjúwmən fíjdbæ̀k bɪkɒ́z ɪt níjdz nów sɛ́prət rɪwɔ́rd mɒ́dəl. súwpərvàjzd fájn-túwnɪŋ ɪnstɛ́d lɜ́rnz frəm sɪ́ŋɡəl ajdíjəl rɪspɒ́nsɪz, ənd DPO ɪz ɔ́fən əplájd ǽftər SFT. rìjɪnfɔ́rsmənt fájn-túwnɪŋ júwzɪz ə ɡréjdər tə rɪwɔ́rd kərɛ́kt ríjzənɪŋ ɒn tǽsks wɪð vɛ́rɪfàjəbəl ǽnsərz.

Question: You want to improve a reasoning model on expert tasks with verifiable answers by rewarding correct results scored by a grader, rather than having it imitate examples. Which method should you use?
Explanation: Reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) is a fine-tuning method for reasoning models, such as o4-mini, in which the model generates answers to training prompts, a grader scores them, and training reinforces the reasoning that leads to high scores. Graders can be deterministic, such as string checks or Python code, or model-based, such as a score model with a rubric, and they define what correct means for your domain. RFT suits complex, expert tasks with clear right answers, such as legal, medical or financial analysis, even with relatively few examples. It is more expensive and complex than supervised fine-tuning, so use it after prompt engineering and SFT have plateaued.
trans_Question: juw wɒ́nt tə ɪmprúwv ə ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəl ɒn ɛ́kspɜrt tǽsks wɪð vɛ́rɪfàjəbəl ǽnsərz baj rɪwɔ́rdɪŋ kərɛ́kt rɪzə́lts skɒ́rɪd baj ə ɡréjdər, rǽðər ðən hǽvɪŋ ɪt ɪ́mətèjt ɪɡzǽmpəlz. wɪ́tʃ mɛ́θəd ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: rìjɪnfɔ́rsmənt fájn-túwnɪŋ (RFT) ɪz ə fájn-túwnɪŋ mɛ́θəd fɔr ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz, sə́tʃ æz o4-mini, ɪn wɪ́tʃ ðə mɒ́dəl dʒɛ́nərèjts ǽnsərz tə tréjnɪŋ prɒ́mpts, ə ɡréjdər skɔ́rz ðɛm, ənd tréjnɪŋ rìjɪnfɔ́rsɪz ðə ríjzənɪŋ ðæt líjdz tə háj skɔ́rz. ɡréjdərz kən bij dɪtɜ̀rmɪnɪ́stɪk, sə́tʃ æz strɪ́ŋ tʃɛ́ks ɔr pájθɒn kówd, ɔr mɒ́dəl-béjst, sə́tʃ æz ə skɔ́r mɒ́dəl wɪð ə rúwbrɪk, ənd ðej dɪfájn wɒ́t kərɛ́kt míjnz fɔr jɔr dowméjn. RFT súwts kəmplɛ́ks, ɛ́kspɜrt tǽsks wɪð klɪ́r rájt ǽnsərz, sə́tʃ æz líjɡəl, mɛ́dɪkəl ɔr fájnæ̀nʃəl ənǽlɪsɪs, íjvən wɪð rɛ́lətɪvlij fjúw ɪɡzǽmpəlz. ɪt ɪz mɔ́r ɪkspɛ́nsɪv ənd kəmplɛ́ks ðən súwpərvàjzd fájn-túwnɪŋ, sów júws ɪt ǽftər prɒ́mpt ɛ̀ndʒɪnɪ́rɪŋ ənd SFT həv plǽtɛəɪd.

Question: You want a small, cheaper model to match a large model's quality on one specific task by training it on the large model's outputs. Which technique is this?
Explanation: Distillation is a technique in which a large, capable teacher model generates high-quality outputs that are used to fine-tune a smaller student model, so the student approaches the teacher's quality on a specific task at lower cost and latency. In Azure OpenAI, stored completions (store set to true) capture production inputs and outputs from the teacher, which you can filter, evaluate and turn into training datasets. The student is then fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning and evaluated against the teacher on the same test set. Distillation works best for narrow, high-volume tasks, because the student generalizes less well outside the trained task.
trans_Question: juw wɒ́nt ə smɔ́l, tʃíjpər mɒ́dəl tə mǽtʃ ə lɑ́rdʒ mɒ́dəlz kwɑ́lɪtij ɒn wə́n spɪsɪ́fɪk tǽsk baj tréjnɪŋ ɪt ɒn ðə lɑ́rdʒ mɒ́dəlz áwtpʊ̀ts. wɪ́tʃ tɛkníjk ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: dɪ̀stɪléjʃən ɪz ə tɛkníjk ɪn wɪ́tʃ ə lɑ́rdʒ, kéjpəbəl tíjtʃər mɒ́dəl dʒɛ́nərèjts háj-kwɑ́lɪtij áwtpʊ̀ts ðǽt ɑr júwzd tə fájn-túwn ə smɔ́lər stúwdənt mɒ́dəl, sów ðə stúwdənt əprówtʃɪz ðə tíjtʃərz kwɑ́lɪtij ɒn ə spɪsɪ́fɪk tǽsk ət lówər kɔ́st ənd léjtənsij. ɪn ǽʒər ówpənAI, stɔ́rd kəmplíjʃənz (stɔ́r sɛ́t tə trúw) kǽptʃər prədə́kʃən ɪ́npʊ̀ts ənd áwtpʊ̀ts frəm ðə tíjtʃər, wɪ́tʃ juw kən fɪ́ltər, ɪvǽljuwèjt ənd tɜ́rn ɪ́ntə tréjnɪŋ déjtəsɛ̀ts. ðə stúwdənt ɪz ðɛ́n fájn-túwnd wɪð súwpərvàjzd fájn-túwnɪŋ ənd ɪvǽljuwèjtɪd əɡɛ́nst ðə tíjtʃər ɒn ðə séjm tɛ́st sɛ́t. dɪ̀stɪléjʃən wɜ́rks bɛ́st fɔr nǽrow, háj-vɒ́ljuwm tǽsks, bɪkɒ́z ðə stúwdənt dʒɛ́nərəlàjzɪz lɛ́s wɛ́l awtsájd ðə tréjnd tǽsk.

Question: A generator model drafts an answer, a critic model scores it against criteria and returns feedback, and the generator revises until the score passes a threshold. Which pattern is this?
Explanation: The evaluator-optimizer loop (also called a generator and critic loop or the reflection pattern) is an iterative pattern in which one model call generates output, another call or model evaluates it against explicit criteria and returns feedback, and the generator revises until a quality threshold is met. Self-critique and self-refine are variants in which the same model critiques and improves its own draft. The pattern improves quality for tasks with clear evaluation criteria, such as writing, code or translation, at the cost of extra calls and latency. Always define stopping criteria, such as a maximum number of iterations and a target score, because a critic can keep finding something to change.
trans_Question: ə dʒɛ́nərèjtər mɒ́dəl drǽfts ən ǽnsər, ə krɪ́tɪk mɒ́dəl skɔ́rz ɪt əɡɛ́nst krajtɪ́rijə ənd rɪtɜ́rnz fíjdbæ̀k, ənd ðə dʒɛ́nərèjtər rɪvájzɪz əntɪ́l ðə skɔ́r pǽsɪz ə θrɛ́ʃòwld. wɪ́tʃ pǽtərn ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: ðij ɪvǽljuwèjtər-ɒ́ptɪmàjzər lúwp (ɔ́lsow kɔ́ld ə dʒɛ́nərèjtər ənd krɪ́tɪk lúwp ɔr ðə rɪflɛ́kʃən pǽtərn) ɪz ən ɪ́tərèjtɪv pǽtərn ɪn wɪ́tʃ wə́n mɒ́dəl kɔ́l dʒɛ́nərèjts áwtpʊ̀t, ənə́ðər kɔ́l ɔr mɒ́dəl ɪvǽljuwèjts ɪt əɡɛ́nst ɪksplɪ́sɪt krajtɪ́rijə ənd rɪtɜ́rnz fíjdbæ̀k, ənd ðə dʒɛ́nərèjtər rɪvájzɪz əntɪ́l ə kwɑ́lɪtij θrɛ́ʃòwld ɪz mɛ́t. sɛ́lf-krɪtíjk ənd sɛ́lf-rɪfájn ɑr vɛ́rijənts ɪn wɪ́tʃ ðə séjm mɒ́dəl krɪ́tɪks ənd ɪ̀mprúwvz ɪts ówn drǽft. ðə pǽtərn ɪ̀mprúwvz kwɑ́lɪtij fɔr tǽsks wɪð klɪ́r ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən krajtɪ́rijə, sə́tʃ æz rájtɪŋ, kówd ɔr trænzléjʃən, ət ðə kɔ́st əv ɛ́kstrə kɔ́lz ənd léjtənsij. ɔ́lwèjz dɪfájn stɒ́pɪŋ krajtɪ́rijə, sə́tʃ æz ə mǽksɪməm nə́mbər əv ɪ̀tə̀réjʃənz ənd ə tɑ́rɡət skɔ́r, bɪkɒ́z ə krɪ́tɪk kən kíjp fájndɪŋ sə́mθɪ̀ŋ tə tʃéjndʒ.

Question: A non-reasoning model makes mistakes on multistep math word problems. Accuracy improves when you instruct it to work through intermediate steps before giving the final answer. Which technique is this?
Explanation: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting asks a model to produce intermediate reasoning steps before its final answer, for example with an instruction to think step by step or with few-shot examples that show worked reasoning. Making reasoning explicit improves accuracy on arithmetic, logic and multistep problems and makes errors easier to inspect. A common practice is to separate the reasoning from the final answer, for example in different sections or JSON fields, so the app can show only the answer. Reasoning models perform this kind of reasoning internally, so explicit CoT instructions are usually unnecessary for them.
trans_Question: ə nɒ́n-ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəl méjks mɪstéjks ɒn mə́ltijstɛp mǽθ wɜ́rd prɒ́bləmz. ǽkjərəsij ɪ̀mprúwvz wɛ́n juw ɪ́nstrəkt ɪt tə wɜ́rk θrúw ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət stɛ́ps bɪfɔ́r ɡɪ́vɪŋ ðə fájnəl ǽnsər. wɪ́tʃ tɛkníjk ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: tʃéjn-əv-θɔ́t (COT) prɒ́mptɪŋ ǽsks ə mɒ́dəl tə prədúws ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət ríjzənɪŋ stɛ́ps bɪfɔ́r ɪts fájnəl ǽnsər, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl wɪð ən ɪ̀nstrə́kʃən tə θɪ́ŋk stɛ́p baj stɛ́p ɔr wɪð fjúw-ʃɒ́t ɪɡzǽmpəlz ðæt ʃów wɜ́rkt ríjzənɪŋ. méjkɪŋ ríjzənɪŋ ɪksplɪ́sɪt ɪ̀mprúwvz ǽkjərəsij ɒn ərɪ́θmətɪk, lɒ́dʒɪk ənd mə́ltijstɛp prɒ́bləmz ənd méjks ɛ́rərz íjzijər tə ɪ̀nspɛ́kt. ə kɒ́mən prǽktɪs ɪz tə sɛ́prət ðə ríjzənɪŋ frəm ðə fájnəl ǽnsər, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl ɪn dɪ́frənt sɛ́kʃənz ɔr JSON fíjldz, sów ðij ǽp kən ʃów ównlij ðij ǽnsər. ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz pərfɔ́rm ðɪs kájnd əv ríjzənɪŋ ɪntɜ́rnəlij, sów ɪksplɪ́sɪt COT ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz ɑr júwʒəwəlij ə̀nnɛ́səsɛ̀rij fɔr ðɛm.

Question: You sample several independent reasoning paths for the same problem at a higher temperature and select the final answer that appears most often. Which technique is this?
Explanation: Self-consistency is a reasoning technique that generates multiple chain-of-thought answers to the same prompt with sampling diversity (higher temperature or the n parameter) and chooses the most frequent final answer by majority vote. It improves accuracy on problems that have one right result, such as math or classification, because random reasoning errors tend not to agree with each other. The trade-off is cost and latency that grow with the number of samples. Tree of Thoughts is a related technique that explores and evaluates branching intermediate steps, backtracking from poor branches, rather than voting on complete answers.
trans_Question: juw sǽmpəl sɛ́vrəl ɪ̀ndɪpɛ́ndənt ríjzənɪŋ pǽðz fɔr ðə séjm prɒ́bləm ət ə hájər tɛ́mprətʃər ənd sɪlɛ́kt ðə fájnəl ǽnsər ðæt əpɪ́rz mówst ɔ́fən. wɪ́tʃ tɛkníjk ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: sɛ́lf-kənsɪ́stənsij ɪz ə ríjzənɪŋ tɛkníjk ðæt dʒɛ́nərèjts mə́ltɪpəl tʃéjn-əv-θɔ́t ǽnsərz tə ðə séjm prɒ́mpt wɪð sǽmplɪŋ dɪvɜ́rsɪtij (hájər tɛ́mprətʃər ɔr ðə n pərǽmətər) ənd tʃúwzɪz ðə mówst fríjkwənt fájnəl ǽnsər baj mədʒɔ́rɪtij vówt. ɪt ɪ̀mprúwvz ǽkjərəsij ɒn prɒ́bləmz ðǽt həv wə́n rájt rɪzə́lt, sə́tʃ æz mǽθ ɔr klæ̀sɪfɪkéjʃən, bɪkɒ́z rǽndəm ríjzənɪŋ ɛ́rərz tɛ́nd nɒ́t tə əɡríj wɪð íjtʃ ə́ðər. ðə tréjd-ɔ́f ɪz kɔ́st ənd léjtənsij ðæt ɡrów wɪð ðə nə́mbər əv sǽmpəlz. tríj əv θɔ́ts ɪz ə rɪléjtɪd tɛkníjk ðæt ɪksplɔ́rz ənd ɪvǽljuwèjts brǽntʃɪŋ ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət stɛ́ps, bǽktrækɪŋ frəm pʊ́r brǽnʃɪz, rǽðər ðən vówtɪŋ ɒn kəmplíjt ǽnsərz.

Question: You move a prompt from GPT-4o to a reasoning model. Which prompt element should you usually remove?
Explanation: Reasoning models, such as the o-series and GPT-5 reasoning models, are trained to reason internally before answering, so prompts that tell them to think step by step or explain their reasoning are unnecessary and can even reduce performance. Prompting guidance for reasoning models is to keep prompts simple and direct, state the goal, constraints and success criteria clearly, use delimiters to separate sections, and try zero-shot before adding examples. They take instructions through developer or system messages and are steered with reasoning effort rather than temperature. Their raw chain of thought isn't returned, but a reasoning summary can be requested for transparency.
