trans_Explanation: ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz, sə́tʃ æz ðij ɒ́-sɪ́rijz ənd GPT-5 ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz, ɑr tréjnd tə ríjzən ɪntɜ́rnəlij bɪfɔ́r ǽnsərɪŋ, sów prɒ́mpts ðæt tɛ́l ðɛm tə θɪ́ŋk stɛ́p baj stɛ́p ɔr ɪkspléjn ðɛr ríjzənɪŋ ɑr ə̀nnɛ́səsɛ̀rij ənd kən íjvən rɪdúws pərfɔ́rməns. prɒ́mptɪŋ ɡájdəns fɔr ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz ɪz tə kíjp prɒ́mpts sɪ́mpəl ənd dɪrɛ́kt, stéjt ðə ɡówl, kənstréjnts ənd səksɛ́s krajtɪ́rijə klɪ́rlij, júws dɪlɪ́mɪtərz tə sɛ́prət sɛ́kʃənz, ənd tráj zɪ́row-ʃɒ́t bɪfɔ́r ǽdɪŋ ɪɡzǽmpəlz. ðej téjk ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz θrúw dɪvɛ́ləpər ɔr sɪ́stəm mɛ́sɪdʒɪz ənd ɑr stɪ́rd wɪð ríjzənɪŋ ɛ́fərt rǽðər ðən tɛ́mprətʃər. ðɛr rɒ́ tʃéjn əv θɔ́t ɪ́zənt rɪtɜ́rnd, bət ə ríjzənɪŋ sə́mərij kən bij rɪkwɛ́stɪd fɔr trænspɛ́rənsij.

Question: You need to assess not only whether final answers are correct but whether the model's intermediate reasoning steps are valid and support the conclusion. What should you implement?
Explanation: Chain-of-thought evaluation assesses the quality of a model's reasoning process, checking whether intermediate steps are logically valid, grounded in the given facts, free of skipped or contradictory steps and actually support the final answer. It is usually implemented with an LLM-as-a-judge and a rubric, sometimes combined with programmatic checks of intermediate results, and it can catch answers that are right for the wrong reasons. For reasoning models, whose raw chain of thought is hidden, you can evaluate reasoning summaries, tool call sequences and the evaluator explanations that AI-assisted evaluators return with each score. Verification passes, in which a separate call fact-checks each claim against sources, complement reasoning evaluation in production.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə əsɛ́s nɒ́t ównlij wɛ́ðər fájnəl ǽnsərz ɑr kərɛ́kt bət wɛ́ðər ðə mɒ́dəlz ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət ríjzənɪŋ stɛ́ps ɑr vǽlɪd ənd səpɔ́rt ðə kənklúwʒən. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw ɪ́mpləmənt?
trans_Explanation: tʃéjn-əv-θɔ́t ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən ǽssɛssɪz ðə kwɑ́lɪtij əv ə mɒ́dəlz ríjzənɪŋ prɒ́sɛs, tʃɛ́kɪŋ wɛ́ðər ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət stɛ́ps ɑr lɒ́dʒɪkəlij vǽlɪd, ɡráwndɪd ɪn ðə ɡɪ́vən fǽkts, fríj əv skɪ́pt ɔr kɒ̀ntrədɪ́ktərij stɛ́ps ənd ǽktʃuwəlij səpɔ́rt ðə fájnəl ǽnsər. ɪt ɪz júwʒəwəlij ɪ́mpləmɛ̀ntɪd wɪð ən LLM-æz-ə-dʒə́dʒ ənd ə rúwbrɪk, sə́mtàjmz kəmbájnd wɪð prɒ̀ɡrəmǽtɪk tʃɛ́ks əv ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət rɪzə́lts, ənd ɪt kən kǽtʃ ǽnsərz ðǽt ɑr rájt fɔr ðə rɔ́ŋ ríjzənz. fɔr ríjzənɪŋ mɒ́dəlz, húwz rɒ́ tʃéjn əv θɔ́t ɪz hɪ́dən, juw kən ɪvǽljuwèjt ríjzənɪŋ sə́mərijz, túwl kɔ́l síjkwənsɪz ənd ðij ɪvǽljuwèjtər ɛ̀ksplənéjʃənz ðæt AI-əsɪ́stɪd ɪvǽljuwèjtərz rɪtɜ́rn wɪð íjtʃ skɔ́r. vɛ̀rɪfɪkéjʃən pǽsɪz, ɪn wɪ́tʃ ə sɛ́prət kɔ́l fǽkt-tʃɛ́ks íjtʃ kléjm əɡɛ́nst sɔ́rsɪz, kɒ́mpləmɛ̀nt ríjzənɪŋ ɪvæ̀ljuwéjʃən ɪn prədə́kʃən.

Question: Which open standard does Microsoft Foundry use to collect and export traces from agents and LLM apps, with semantic conventions for generative AI?
Explanation: OpenTelemetry (OTel) is the open, vendor-neutral observability standard of APIs, SDKs and protocols for traces, metrics and logs, and Foundry uses it with the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI (gen_ai.* attributes) so traces are consistent across the Foundry SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangChain, LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK. A trace represents one end-to-end request and is made of spans for individual operations (such as invoke_agent, chat and execute_tool) with attributes and events, linked by W3C Trace Context. Foundry stores traces in the Application Insights resource connected to the project, where retention and sampling follow your Application Insights configuration. Server-side traces are captured automatically for Foundry agents, client-side tracing extends visibility into your own code, and the GenAI conventions still have Development status, so names can change.
trans_Question: wɪ́tʃ ówpən stǽndərd dəz májkrəsɔ̀ft fáwndrij júws tə kəlɛ́kt ənd ɛ́kspɔ̀rt tréjsɪz frəm éjdʒənts ənd LLM ǽps, wɪð sɪmǽntɪk kənvɛ́nʃənz fɔr dʒɛ́nərətɪv AI?
trans_Explanation: ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij (ówtɛl) ɪz ðij ówpən, vɛ́ndər-núwtrəl əbzɜ̀rvəbɪ́lɪtij stǽndərd əv APIz, SDKz ənd prɒ́tɒkɒls fɔr tréjsɪz, mɛ́trɪks ənd lɔ́ɡz, ənd fáwndrij júwzɪz ɪt wɪð ðij ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij sɪmǽntɪk kənvɛ́nʃənz fɔr dʒɛ́nərətɪv AI (gen_ai.* ǽtrɪbjùwts) sów tréjsɪz ɑr kənsɪ́stənt əkrɔ́s ðə fáwndrij SDK, májkrəsɔ̀ft éjdʒənt fréjmwɜ̀rk, lǽŋtʃèjn, lǽŋɡræ̀f ənd ðij ówpənAI éjdʒənts SDK. ə tréjs rɛ̀prɪzɛ́nts wə́n ɛ́nd-tə-ɛ́nd rɪkwɛ́st ənd ɪz méjd əv spǽnz fɔr ɪ̀ndɪvɪ́dʒuwəl ɒ̀pəréjʃənz (sə́tʃ æz invoke_agent, tʃǽt ənd execute_tool) wɪð ǽtrɪbjùwts ənd ɪvɛ́nts, lɪ́ŋkt baj W3C tréjs kɒ́ntɛkst. fáwndrij stɔ́rz tréjsɪz ɪn ðij æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts ríjsɔrs kənɛ́ktɪd tə ðə prɒ́dʒɛkt, wɛ́r rɪtɛ́nʃən ənd sǽmplɪŋ fɒ́low jɔr æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts kənfɪ̀ɡjəréjʃən. sɜ́rvər-sájd tréjsɪz ɑr kǽptʃərd ɔ̀təmǽtɪkəlij fɔr fáwndrij éjdʒənts, klájənt-sájd tréjsɪŋ ɪkstɛ́ndz vɪ̀zɪbɪ́lɪtij ɪ́ntə jɔr ówn kówd, ənd ðə dʒɛ́nAI kənvɛ́nʃənz stɪ́l həv dɪvɛ́ləpmənt stéjtəs, sów néjmz kən tʃéjndʒ.

Question: In Python, which function sends OpenTelemetry traces from your app to the Application Insights resource connected to your Foundry project?
Explanation: The configure_azure_monitor() function from the azure-monitor-opentelemetry package (the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distro) sets up OpenTelemetry exporters that send traces, metrics and logs to Application Insights by using a connection string. For a Foundry project, you can get the string with project.telemetry.get_application_insights_connection_string() or set APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING, and then instrument Foundry SDK and OpenAI calls (in Python with AIProjectInstrumentor, after opting in by setting AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING to true). Traces typically appear in the Foundry portal tracing view within a few minutes, and viewing them requires read access to the underlying Log Analytics data. For local debugging, a console or OTLP exporter (for example to the Aspire Dashboard or the Foundry Toolkit for VS Code) can replace Azure Monitor.
trans_Question: ɪn pájθɒn, wɪ́tʃ fə́ŋkʃən sɛ́ndz ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij tréjsɪz frəm jɔr ǽp tə ðij æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts ríjsɔrs kənɛ́ktɪd tə jɔr fáwndrij prɒ́dʒɛkt?
trans_Explanation: ðə configure_azure_monitor() fə́ŋkʃən frəm ðij ǽʒər-mɒ́nɪtər-ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij pǽkɪdʒ (ðij ǽʒər mɒ́nɪtər ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij dɪ́strɒ) sɛ́ts ə́p ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij ɛkspɔ́rtərz ðæt sɛ́nd tréjsɪz, mɛ́trɪks ənd lɔ́ɡz tə æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts baj júwzɪŋ ə kənɛ́kʃən strɪ́ŋ. fɔr ə fáwndrij prɒ́dʒɛkt, juw kən ɡɛ́t ðə strɪ́ŋ wɪð project.telemetry.get_application_insights_connection_string() ɔr sɛ́t APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING, ənd ðɛ́n ɪ́nstrəmənt fáwndrij SDK ənd ówpənAI kɔ́lz (ɪn pájθɒn wɪð AIProjectInstrumentor, ǽftər ɒ́ptɪŋ ɪn baj sɛ́tɪŋ AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING tə trúw). tréjsɪz tɪ́pɪkəlij əpɪ́r ɪn ðə fáwndrij pɔ́rtəl tréjsɪŋ vjúw wɪðɪ́n ə fjúw mɪ́nəts, ənd vjúwɪŋ ðɛm rɪkwájərz ríjd ǽksɛ̀s tə ðij ə̀ndərlájɪŋ lɔ́ɡ æ̀nəlɪ́tɪks déjtə. fɔr lówkəl dijbə́ɡɪŋ, ə kɒ́nsɒl ɔr OTLP ɪkspɔ́rtər (fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl tə ðij ǽspɪr dǽʃbɔ̀rd ɔr ðə fáwndrij túwlkɪt fɔr VS kówd) kən rɪpléjs ǽʒər mɒ́nɪtər.

Question: Traces show token counts and latency but not the prompt and response text. You need message content in traces in a development environment. What should you enable?
Explanation: Content recording is a tracing setting that captures message contents and tool call arguments and results in GenAI spans, and it is off by default because this data can include personal or confidential information. In Python you enable it by setting OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT to true or by passing enable_content_recording when instrumenting (older Azure samples use AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED). Microsoft recommends enabling it only in development or with redaction, never placing secrets or tokens in prompts or span attributes, and applying the same access controls and retention policies to traces as to production logs. Functions you decorate for custom tracing record their parameters and return values regardless of this setting.
trans_Question: tréjsɪz ʃów tówkən káwnts ənd léjtənsij bət nɒ́t ðə prɒ́mpt ənd rɪspɒ́ns tɛ́kst. juw níjd mɛ́sɪdʒ kɒ́ntɛnt ɪn tréjsɪz ɪn ə dɪvɛ́ləpmənt ɪnvájərənmənt. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw ɪnéjbəl?
trans_Explanation: kɒ́ntɛnt rɪkɔ́rdɪŋ ɪz ə tréjsɪŋ sɛ́tɪŋ ðæt kǽptʃərz mɛ́sɪdʒ kɒ́ntɛnts ənd túwl kɔ́l ɑ́rɡjəmənts ənd rɪzə́lts ɪn dʒɛ́nAI spǽnz, ənd ɪt ɪz ɔ́f baj dɪfɔ́lt bɪkɒ́z ðɪs déjtə kən ɪnklúwd pɜ́rsənəl ɔr kɒ̀nfɪdɛ́nʃəl ɪ̀nfərméjʃən. ɪn pájθɒn juw ɪnéjbəl ɪt baj sɛ́tɪŋ OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT tə trúw ɔr baj pǽsɪŋ enable_content_recording wɛ́n ɪ́nstrəmɛntɪŋ (ówldər ǽʒər sǽmpəlz júws AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED). májkrəsɔ̀ft rɛ̀kəmɛ́ndz ɪnéjblɪŋ ɪt ównlij ɪn dɪvɛ́ləpmənt ɔr wɪð rɪdǽkʃən, nɛ́vər pléjsɪŋ síjkrəts ɔr tówkənz ɪn prɒ́mpts ɔr spǽn ǽtrɪbjùwts, ənd əplájɪŋ ðə séjm ǽksɛ̀s kəntrówlz ənd rɪtɛ́nʃən pɒ́lɪsijz tə tréjsɪz æz tə prədə́kʃən lɔ́ɡz. fə́ŋkʃənz juw dɛ́kərèjt fɔr kə́stəm tréjsɪŋ rɛ́kərd ðɛr pərǽmətərz ənd rɪtɜ́rn vǽljuwz rɪɡɑ́rdləs əv ðɪs sɛ́tɪŋ.

Question: Which OpenTelemetry span attributes record the input and output token counts of a model call?
Explanation: Token analytics in traces relies on the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, where gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens record the tokens consumed by each model call. Other common attributes include gen_ai.operation.name (such as chat, invoke_agent or execute_tool), gen_ai.request.model and gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.agent.name, and tool attributes such as gen_ai.tool.call.arguments. Aggregating usage attributes by agent, model, user or feature in Application Insights (with KQL) shows where tokens and costs go, and reveals verbose prompts, long histories or runaway tool loops. Token usage is also summarized on the Agent Monitoring Dashboard and in Azure Monitor metrics for each deployment.
trans_Question: wɪ́tʃ ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij spǽn ǽtrɪbjùwts rɛ́kərd ðij ɪ́npʊ̀t ənd áwtpʊ̀t tówkən káwnts əv ə mɒ́dəl kɔ́l?
trans_Explanation: tówkən æ̀nəlɪ́tɪks ɪn tréjsɪz rɪlájz ɒn ðij ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij dʒɛ́nAI sɪmǽntɪk kənvɛ́nʃənz, wɛ́r gen_ai.usage.input_tokens ənd gen_ai.usage.output_tokens rɛ́kərd ðə tówkənz kənsúwmd baj íjtʃ mɒ́dəl kɔ́l. ə́ðər kɒ́mən ǽtrɪbjùwts ɪnklúwd gen_ai.operation.name (sə́tʃ æz tʃǽt, invoke_agent ɔr execute_tool), gen_ai.request.model ənd gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.agent.name, ənd túwl ǽtrɪbjùwts sə́tʃ æz gen_ai.tool.call.arguments. ǽɡɡrɛɡætɪŋ júwsɪdʒ ǽtrɪbjùwts baj éjdʒənt, mɒ́dəl, júwzər ɔr fíjtʃər ɪn æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts (wɪð KQL) ʃówz wɛ́r tówkənz ənd kɔ́sts ɡów, ənd rɪvíjlz vɜ́rbows prɒ́mpts, lɔ́ŋ hɪ́stərijz ɔr rə́nəwèj túwl lúwps. tówkən júwsɪdʒ ɪz ɔ́lsow sə́məràjzd ɒn ðij éjdʒənt mɒ́nɪtərɪŋ dǽʃbɔ̀rd ənd ɪn ǽʒər mɒ́nɪtər mɛ́trɪks fɔr íjtʃ dɪplɔ́jmənt.

Question: Users say a chat app feels slow before any text appears, although total generation time is acceptable. Which latency metric should you analyze?
Explanation: Time to first token (TTFT) is the delay between sending a request and receiving the first generated token, which determines how responsive a streaming app feels. A latency breakdown separates TTFT, generation speed (tokens per second), end-to-end latency and the time spent in each span, such as retrieval, tool calls and model calls, so you can see which step is slow. TTFT grows with long prompts, reasoning tokens, guardrail processing and queuing under load, and it can be reduced with streaming, shorter or cached prompts, lower reasoning effort, smaller models or provisioned throughput. Traces in Application Insights show per-span durations for this analysis.
trans_Question: júwzərz séj ə tʃǽt ǽp fíjlz slów bɪfɔ́r ɛ́nij tɛ́kst əpɪ́rz, ɔ̀lðów tówtəl dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən tájm ɪz əksɛ́ptəbəl. wɪ́tʃ léjtənsij mɛ́trɪk ʃʊd juw ǽnəlàjz?
trans_Explanation: tájm tə fɜ́rst tówkən (TTFT) ɪz ðə dɪléj bɪtwíjn sɛ́ndɪŋ ə rɪkwɛ́st ənd rɪsíjvɪŋ ðə fɜ́rst dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd tówkən, wɪ́tʃ dɪtɜ́rmɪnz háw rɛ́spɒnsɪv ə stríjmɪŋ ǽp fíjlz. ə léjtənsij bréjkdàwn sɛ́pərèjts TTFT, dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən spíjd (tówkənz pə́r sɛ́kənd), ɛ́nd-tə-ɛ́nd léjtənsij ənd ðə tájm spɛ́nt ɪn íjtʃ spǽn, sə́tʃ æz rɪtríjvəl, túwl kɔ́lz ənd mɒ́dəl kɔ́lz, sów juw kən síj wɪ́tʃ stɛ́p ɪz slów. TTFT ɡrówz wɪð lɔ́ŋ prɒ́mpts, ríjzənɪŋ tówkənz, ɡɑ́rdrèjl prɒ́sɛsɪŋ ənd kwɛ́əɪŋ ə́ndər lówd, ənd ɪt kən bij rɪdúwst wɪð stríjmɪŋ, ʃɔ́rtər ɔr kǽʃt prɒ́mpts, lówər ríjzənɪŋ ɛ́fərt, smɔ́lər mɒ́dəlz ɔr prəvɪ́ʒənd θrúwpʊ̀t. tréjsɪz ɪn æ̀plɪkéjʃən ɪ́nsàjts ʃów pə́r-spǽn dʊréjʃənz fɔr ðɪs ənǽlɪsɪs.

Question: In an agent trace, you need to find out which tool call caused a slow response. Which spans should you inspect?
Explanation: An execute_tool span is the child span that the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions use for each tool execution, recording the tool name, its arguments (gen_ai.tool.call.arguments), its result (gen_ai.tool.call.result) and its duration. In a typical agent trace, an invoke_agent span wraps the whole run, with child spans for model calls (chat), planning (plan), memory operations (such as search_memory) and tool executions (execute_tool), and multi-agent systems add invoke_workflow spans. Comparing durations across these child spans gives a latency breakdown that pinpoints slow tools, model calls or retrieval. Failed spans and exception events in the same trace support root cause analysis of errors.
trans_Question: ɪn ən éjdʒənt tréjs, juw níjd tə fájnd áwt wɪ́tʃ túwl kɔ́l kɔ́zd ə slów rɪspɒ́ns. wɪ́tʃ spǽnz ʃʊd juw ɪ̀nspɛ́kt?
trans_Explanation: ən execute_tool spǽn ɪz ðə tʃájld spǽn ðət ðij ówpəntɛ̀ləmɛtrij dʒɛ́nAI kənvɛ́nʃənz júws fɔr íjtʃ túwl ɪ̀ksəkjúwʃən, rɪkɔ́rdɪŋ ðə túwl néjm, ɪts ɑ́rɡjəmənts (gen_ai.tool.call.arguments), ɪts rɪzə́lt (gen_ai.tool.call.result) ənd ɪts dʊréjʃən. ɪn ə tɪ́pɪkəl éjdʒənt tréjs, ən invoke_agent spǽn rǽps ðə hówl rə́n, wɪð tʃájld spǽnz fɔr mɒ́dəl kɔ́lz (tʃǽt), plǽnɪŋ (plǽn), mɛ́mrij ɒ̀pəréjʃənz (sə́tʃ æz search_memory) ənd túwl ɛ̀ksɪkjúwʃənz (execute_tool), ənd mə́ltij-éjdʒənt sɪ́stəmz ǽd invoke_workflow spǽnz. kəmpɛ́rɪŋ dʊréjʃənz əkrɔ́s ðijz tʃájld spǽnz ɡɪ́vz ə léjtənsij bréjkdàwn ðæt pɪ́npɔjnts slów túwlz, mɒ́dəl kɔ́lz ɔr rɪtríjvəl. féjld spǽnz ənd ɪksɛ́pʃən ɪvɛ́nts ɪn ðə séjm tréjs səpɔ́rt rúwt kɔ́z ənǽlɪsɪs əv ɛ́rərz.

Question: You want a single deployment that analyzes each prompt and routes it in real time to the most suitable underlying model to balance cost and quality. What should you deploy?
Explanation: Model router is a trained model, deployed like any other Foundry model, that routes each prompt in real time to the most suitable underlying LLM based on complexity, reasoning needs and task type, so simple prompts go to smaller, cheaper models and hard ones to more capable models. It is called through a single deployment name with the usual chat or Responses APIs, the response shows which underlying model answered, and it is available with Global Standard and Data Zone Standard deployments. You can restrict routing to a model subset, and failover to other models in the subset is enabled by default, so include at least two models. The effective context window is limited by the smallest underlying model, and routing decisions use only the text input.
trans_Question: juw wɒ́nt ə sɪ́ŋɡəl dɪplɔ́jmənt ðæt ǽnəlàjzɪz íjtʃ prɒ́mpt ənd rúwts ɪt ɪn ríjəl tájm tə ðə mówst súwtəbəl ə̀ndərlájɪŋ mɒ́dəl tə bǽləns kɔ́st ənd kwɑ́lɪtij. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw dɪplɔ́j?
trans_Explanation: mɒ́dəl ráwtər ɪz ə tréjnd mɒ́dəl, dɪplɔ́jd lájk ɛ́nij ə́ðər fáwndrij mɒ́dəl, ðæt rúwts íjtʃ prɒ́mpt ɪn ríjəl tájm tə ðə mówst súwtəbəl ə̀ndərlájɪŋ LLM béjst ɒn kəmplɛ́ksɪtij, ríjzənɪŋ níjdz ənd tǽsk tájp, sów sɪ́mpəl prɒ́mpts ɡów tə smɔ́lər, tʃíjpər mɒ́dəlz ənd hɑ́rd wə́nz tə mɔ́r kéjpəbəl mɒ́dəlz. ɪt ɪz kɔ́ld θrúw ə sɪ́ŋɡəl dɪplɔ́jmənt néjm wɪð ðə júwʒəwəl tʃǽt ɔr rɪspɒ́nsɪz APIz, ðə rɪspɒ́ns ʃówz wɪ́tʃ ə̀ndərlájɪŋ mɒ́dəl ǽnsərd, ənd ɪt ɪz əvéjləbəl wɪð ɡlówbəl stǽndərd ənd déjtə zówn stǽndərd dɪplɔ́jmənts. juw kən rɪstrɪ́kt ráwtɪŋ tə ə mɒ́dəl sə́bsɛ̀t, ənd féjlòwvər tə ə́ðər mɒ́dəlz ɪn ðə sə́bsɛ̀t ɪz ɪnéjbəld baj dɪfɔ́lt, sów ɪnklúwd ət líjst túw mɒ́dəlz. ðij ɪfɛ́ktɪv kɒ́ntɛkst wɪ́ndow ɪz lɪ́mɪtɪd baj ðə smɔ́ləst ə̀ndərlájɪŋ mɒ́dəl, ənd ráwtɪŋ dɪsɪ́ʒənz júws ównlij ðə tɛ́kst ɪ́npʊ̀t.

Question: Your high-volume, budget-sensitive app uses model router. You want routing to favor cheaper models within a wider quality band. Which routing mode should you choose?
Explanation: Routing mode is a model router setting, chosen in a custom deployment, that controls the trade-off between cost and quality. Balanced, the default, considers models within a small quality range (about 1% to 2%) of the best model for each prompt and picks the most cost-effective one, Cost widens that band (about 5% to 6%) to save more, and Quality always picks the highest-rated model regardless of cost. A model subset limits which underlying models can be chosen and also serves as the failover set, and new base models join a subset only when you add them. Monitor routed models, latency and cost to confirm that the mode fits the workload.
trans_Question: jɔr háj-vɒ́ljuwm, bə́dʒət-sɛ́nsɪtɪv ǽp júwzɪz mɒ́dəl ráwtər. juw wɒ́nt ráwtɪŋ tə féjvər tʃíjpər mɒ́dəlz wɪðɪ́n ə wájdər kwɑ́lɪtij bǽnd. wɪ́tʃ ráwtɪŋ mówd ʃʊd juw tʃúwz?
trans_Explanation: ráwtɪŋ mówd ɪz ə mɒ́dəl ráwtər sɛ́tɪŋ, tʃówzən ɪn ə kə́stəm dɪplɔ́jmənt, ðæt kəntrówlz ðə tréjd-ɔ́f bɪtwíjn kɔ́st ənd kwɑ́lɪtij. bǽlənst, ðə dɪfɔ́lt, kənsɪ́dərz mɒ́dəlz wɪðɪ́n ə smɔ́l kwɑ́lɪtij réjndʒ (əbáwt 1% tə 2%) əv ðə bɛ́st mɒ́dəl fɔr íjtʃ prɒ́mpt ənd pɪ́ks ðə mówst kɔ́st-ɪfɛ́ktɪv wə́n, kɔ́st wɪ́dɛns ðæt bǽnd (əbáwt 5% tə 6%) tə séjv mɔ́r, ənd kwɑ́lɪtij ɔ́lwèjz pɪ́ks ðə hájəst-réjtɪd mɒ́dəl rɪɡɑ́rdləs əv kɔ́st. ə mɒ́dəl sə́bsɛ̀t lɪ́mɪts wɪ́tʃ ə̀ndərlájɪŋ mɒ́dəlz kən bij tʃówzən ənd ɔ́lsow sɜ́rvz æz ðə féjlòwvər sɛ́t, ənd núw béjs mɒ́dəlz dʒɔ́jn ə sə́bsɛ̀t ównlij wɛ́n juw ǽd ðɛm. mɒ́nɪtər rúwtɪd mɒ́dəlz, léjtənsij ənd kɔ́st tə kənfɜ́rm ðət ðə mówd fɪ́ts ðə wɜ́rklòwd.

Question: Loan decisions must follow strict, auditable eligibility rules, but applicant details arrive as free-text documents. Which design should you use?
Explanation: A hybrid LLM and rules engine design uses the LLM for what it does best, such as understanding unstructured text, extracting fields into structured JSON or drafting explanations, and uses deterministic business rules or a rules engine for decisions that must be exact, consistent and auditable. This keeps regulated decisions explainable and testable while still automating language-heavy steps. Typical implementations validate the LLM's structured output against a schema and then evaluate rules in code, Azure Logic Apps, Power Automate or a dedicated rules engine. Uncertain or exceptional cases are routed to human review.
trans_Question: lówn dɪsɪ́ʒənz məst fɒ́low strɪ́kt, ɔ́dɪtəbəl ɛ̀lɪdʒɪbɪ́lɪtij rúwlz, bət ǽplɪkənt dɪtéjlz ərájv æz fríj-tɛ́kst dɒ́kjəmənts. wɪ́tʃ dɪzájn ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: ə hájbrɪd LLM ənd rúwlz ɛ́ndʒɪn dɪzájn júwzɪz ðə LLM fɔr wɒ́t ɪt dəz bɛ́st, sə́tʃ æz ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ ənstrə́ktʃərd tɛ́kst, ɪkstrǽktɪŋ fíjldz ɪ́ntə strə́ktʃərd JSON ɔr drǽftɪŋ ɛ̀ksplənéjʃənz, ənd júwzɪz dɪtɜ̀rmɪnɪ́stɪk bɪ́znəs rúwlz ɔr ə rúwlz ɛ́ndʒɪn fɔr dɪsɪ́ʒənz ðæt məst bij ɪɡzǽkt, kənsɪ́stənt ənd ɔ́dɪtəbəl. ðɪs kíjps rɛ́ɡjəlèjtɪd dɪsɪ́ʒənz ɛ́ksplejnəbəl ənd tɛ́stəbəl wájl stɪ́l ɔ́təmèjtɪŋ lǽŋɡwɪdʒ-hɛ́vij stɛ́ps. tɪ́pɪkəl ɪ́mplɛmɛntætɪɒns vǽlɪdèjt ðə LLMz strə́ktʃərd áwtpʊ̀t əɡɛ́nst ə skíjmə ənd ðɛ́n ɪvǽljuwèjt rúwlz ɪn kówd, ǽʒər lɒ́dʒɪk ǽps, páwər ɔ́tə̀mèjt ɔr ə dɛ́dɪkèjtɪd rúwlz ɛ́ndʒɪn. ə̀nsɜ́rtən ɔr ɪksɛ́pʃənəl kéjsɪz ɑr rúwtɪd tə hjúwmən rɪvjúw.

Question: To cut costs, each request first goes to a small model, and only requests whose answer fails a confidence or quality check are escalated to a larger model. Which pattern is this?
Explanation: Model cascading is a multi-model pattern in which requests start with a fast, inexpensive model and are escalated to progressively more capable and expensive models only when a check fails, such as low confidence, a failed validation, a guardrail flag or a poor evaluator score. It reduces average cost and latency when most requests are easy, at the price of extra latency for escalated requests and the need for a reliable check. Model router automates a similar cost and quality trade-off by choosing a model before generation, while fallback deployments switch to another model or region when a call fails with errors such as 429 or 5xx. Ensembles instead run several models on the same request and combine their outputs.
trans_Question: tə kə́t kɔ́sts, íjtʃ rɪkwɛ́st fɜ́rst ɡówz tə ə smɔ́l mɒ́dəl, ənd ównlij rɪkwɛ́sts húwz ǽnsər féjlz ə kɒ́nfɪdəns ɔr kwɑ́lɪtij tʃɛ́k ɑr ɛ́skəlèjtɪd tə ə lɑ́rdʒər mɒ́dəl. wɪ́tʃ pǽtərn ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: mɒ́dəl kæskéjdɪŋ ɪz ə mə́ltij-mɒ́dəl pǽtərn ɪn wɪ́tʃ rɪkwɛ́sts stɑ́rt wɪð ə fǽst, ɪ̀nɪkspɛ́nsɪv mɒ́dəl ənd ɑr ɛ́skəlèjtɪd tə prəɡrɛ́sɪvlij mɔ́r kéjpəbəl ənd ɪkspɛ́nsɪv mɒ́dəlz ównlij wɛ́n ə tʃɛ́k féjlz, sə́tʃ æz lów kɒ́nfɪdəns, ə féjld væ̀lɪdéjʃən, ə ɡɑ́rdrèjl flǽɡ ɔr ə pʊ́r ɪvǽljuwèjtər skɔ́r. ɪt rɪdúwsɪz ǽvrɪdʒ kɔ́st ənd léjtənsij wɛ́n mówst rɪkwɛ́sts ɑr íjzij, ət ðə prájs əv ɛ́kstrə léjtənsij fɔr ɛ́skəlèjtɪd rɪkwɛ́sts ənd ðə níjd fɔr ə rɪlájəbəl tʃɛ́k. mɒ́dəl ráwtər ɔ́tə̀mèjts ə sɪ́mɪlər kɔ́st ənd kwɑ́lɪtij tréjd-ɔ́f baj tʃúwzɪŋ ə mɒ́dəl bɪfɔ́r dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən, wájl fɔ́lbæ̀k dɪplɔ́jmənts swɪ́tʃ tə ənə́ðər mɒ́dəl ɔr ríjdʒən wɛ́n ə kɔ́l féjlz wɪð ɛ́rərz sə́tʃ æz 429 ɔr 5xx. ɑnsɑ́mbəl ɪnstɛ́d rə́n sɛ́vrəl mɒ́dəlz ɒn ðə séjm rɪkwɛ́st ənd kɒ́mbajn ðɛr áwtpʊ̀ts.

Question: A lightweight classifier labels each incoming request as billing, technical or general and sends it to a specialized model, prompt or flow for that category. Which pattern is this?
Explanation: Intent-based routing is an orchestration pattern in which a classification step, using a small LLM, a fine-tuned classifier, embedding similarity (semantic routing) or rules, identifies what a request is about and dispatches it to the model, prompt, agent or workflow specialized for that intent. Each path can then use the cheapest adequate model and focused instructions, which usually improves accuracy compared with one general prompt that tries to handle everything. Guard models can run in the same position to block or flag unsafe or out-of-scope requests before any expensive call. Azure Language offers related prebuilt options, such as conversational language understanding, orchestration workflow and an Intent Routing agent.
trans_Question: ə lájtwèjt klǽsəfàjər léjbəlz íjtʃ ɪ́nkə̀mɪŋ rɪkwɛ́st æz bɪ́lɪŋ, tɛ́knɪkəl ɔr dʒɛ́nərəl ənd sɛ́ndz ɪt tə ə spɛ́ʃəlàjzd mɒ́dəl, prɒ́mpt ɔr flów fɔr ðæt kǽtɪɡɔ̀rij. wɪ́tʃ pǽtərn ɪz ðɪs?
trans_Explanation: ɪntɛ́nt-béjst ráwtɪŋ ɪz ən ɔ̀rkɪstréjʃən pǽtərn ɪn wɪ́tʃ ə klæ̀sɪfɪkéjʃən stɛ́p, júwzɪŋ ə smɔ́l LLM, ə fájn-túwnd klǽsəfàjər, ɪmbɛ́dɪŋ sɪ̀mɪlɛ́rɪtij (sɪmǽntɪk ráwtɪŋ) ɔr rúwlz, ajdɛ́ntɪfàjz wɒ́t ə rɪkwɛ́st ɪz əbáwt ənd dɪspǽtʃɪz ɪt tə ðə mɒ́dəl, prɒ́mpt, éjdʒənt ɔr wɜ́rkflòw spɛ́ʃəlàjzd fɔr ðæt ɪntɛ́nt. íjtʃ pǽθ kən ðɛ́n júws ðə tʃíjpəst ǽdɪkwət mɒ́dəl ənd fówkəst ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz, wɪ́tʃ júwʒəwəlij ɪ̀mprúwvz ǽkjərəsij kəmpɛ́rd wɪð wə́n dʒɛ́nərəl prɒ́mpt ðæt trájz tə hǽndəl ɛ́vrɪθɪ̀ŋ. ɡɑ́rd mɒ́dəlz kən rə́n ɪn ðə séjm pəzɪ́ʃən tə blɒ́k ɔr flǽɡ ə̀nséjf ɔr áwt-əv-skówp rɪkwɛ́sts bɪfɔ́r ɛ́nij ɪkspɛ́nsɪv kɔ́l. ǽʒər lǽŋɡwɪdʒ ɔ́fərz rɪléjtɪd prìjbɪ́lt ɒ́pʃənz, sə́tʃ æz kɒ̀nvərséjʃənəl lǽŋɡwɪdʒ ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ, ɔ̀rkɪstréjʃən wɜ́rkflòw ənd ən ɪntɛ́nt ráwtɪŋ éjdʒənt.

Question: A new Foundry app must generate marketing images from text prompts, and DALL-E 3 is no longer available for new deployments. Which model family should you use?
Explanation: The GPT-image series (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-1 and gpt-image-1-mini) are OpenAI's natively multimodal image models in Foundry, which create images from text prompts and edit or combine input images, with strong instruction following and text rendering. On Azure, gpt-image-2 is generally available while the gpt-image-1 series requires a limited access application, and DALL-E 3 was retired in March 2026. They are called through the Images API (images.generate for text-to-image and images.edit for image-to-image) or through the image generation tool in the Responses API and Foundry agents. Foundry also offers non-OpenAI image models, such as FLUX models from Black Forest Labs, through the model catalog.
trans_Question: ə núw fáwndrij ǽp məst dʒɛ́nərèjt mɑ́rkətɪŋ ɪ́mɪdʒɪz frəm tɛ́kst prɒ́mpts, ənd DALL-E 3 ɪz nów lɔ́ŋɡər əvéjləbəl fɔr núw dɪplɔ́jmənts. wɪ́tʃ mɒ́dəl fǽmlij ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: ðə GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ sɪ́rijz (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-1 ənd gpt-image-1-mini) ɑr ówpənAIz néjtɪvlij mə̀ltijmówdəl ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz ɪn fáwndrij, wɪ́tʃ krijéjt ɪ́mɪdʒɪz frəm tɛ́kst prɒ́mpts ənd ɛ́dɪt ɔr kɒ́mbajn ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒɪz, wɪð strɔ́ŋ ɪ̀nstrə́kʃən fɒ́lowɪŋ ənd tɛ́kst rɛ́ndərɪŋ. ɒn ǽʒər, gpt-image-2 ɪz dʒɛ́nərəlij əvéjləbəl wájl ðə gpt-image-1 sɪ́rijz rɪkwájərz ə lɪ́mɪtɪd ǽksɛ̀s æ̀plɪkéjʃən, ənd DALL-E 3 wəz rɪtájərd ɪn mɑ́rtʃ 2026. ðej ɑr kɔ́ld θrúw ðij ɪ́mɪdʒɪz API (images.generate fɔr tɛ́kst-tə-ɪ́mɪdʒ ənd images.edit fɔr ɪ́mɪdʒ-tə-ɪ́mɪdʒ) ɔr θrúw ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən túwl ɪn ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API ənd fáwndrij éjdʒənts. fáwndrij ɔ́lsow ɔ́fərz nɒ́n-ówpənAI ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz, sə́tʃ æz FLUX mɒ́dəlz frəm blǽk fɔ́rɪst lǽbz, θrúw ðə mɒ́dəl kǽtəlɔ̀ɡ.

Question: Your app calls images.generate on a GPT-image deployment. In which form is the generated image returned?
Explanation: Image generation responses from GPT-image models return each image as base64-encoded data in the b64_json field, because these models don't support the response_format parameter and never return URLs, so the app decodes the data and stores it itself. The legacy DALL-E models could return either a temporary URL or b64_json and also returned a revised_prompt showing how the service rewrote the prompt. A request can generate between 1 and 10 images (n), and setting stream to true with partial_images (0 to 3) returns intermediate images while the final one renders. If the prompt or output is flagged by content filtering, the call fails with a content filter error instead of returning an image.
trans_Question: jɔr ǽp kɔ́lz images.generate ɒn ə GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ dɪplɔ́jmənt. ɪn wɪ́tʃ fɔ́rm ɪz ðə dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd ɪ́mɪdʒ rɪtɜ́rnd?
trans_Explanation: ɪ́mɪdʒ dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən rɪspɒ́nsɪz frəm GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz rɪtɜ́rn íjtʃ ɪ́mɪdʒ æz Base64-ɪnkówdɪd déjtə ɪn ðə b64_json fíjld, bɪkɒ́z ðijz mɒ́dəlz dównt səpɔ́rt ðə response_format pərǽmətər ənd nɛ́vər rɪtɜ́rn URLz, sów ðij ǽp dɛ́kɒdɪz ðə déjtə ənd stɔ́rz ɪt ɪtsɛ́lf. ðə lɛ́ɡəsij DALL-E mɒ́dəlz kʊd rɪtɜ́rn íjðər ə tɛ́mpərɛ̀rij URL ɔr b64_json ənd ɔ́lsow rɪtɜ́rnd ə revised_prompt ʃówɪŋ háw ðə sɜ́rvɪs rɛ́rɒt ðə prɒ́mpt. ə rɪkwɛ́st kən dʒɛ́nərèjt bɪtwíjn 1 ənd 10 ɪ́mɪdʒɪz (n), ənd sɛ́tɪŋ stríjm tə trúw wɪð partial_images (0 tə 3) rɪtɜ́rnz ɪ̀ntərmíjdijət ɪ́mɪdʒɪz wájl ðə fájnəl wə́n rɛ́ndərz. ɪf ðə prɒ́mpt ɔr áwtpʊ̀t ɪz flǽɡd baj kɒ́ntɛnt fɪ́ltərɪŋ, ðə kɔ́l féjlz wɪð ə kɒ́ntɛnt fɪ́ltər ɛ́rər ɪnstɛ́d əv rɪtɜ́rnɪŋ ən ɪ́mɪdʒ.

Question: A Foundry agent must create photorealistic product images from the conversation context and refine them over several turns. What should you add to the agent?
Explanation: The image generation tool lets a model in the Responses API or a Foundry agent create or edit images as part of a conversation by using a GPT-image model deployment, so the model writes the image prompt from context and refines the image across turns. The model decides when to call the tool, and outputs arrive as image generation call items that contain base64 image data, with optional partial images when streaming. Multi-turn editing works by referring to earlier image outputs or responses rather than re-uploading files. For standalone, single-shot generation without a conversation, call the Images API directly.
trans_Question: ə fáwndrij éjdʒənt məst krijéjt fòwtòwrìjəlɪ́stɪk prɒ́dəkt ɪ́mɪdʒɪz frəm ðə kɒ̀nvərséjʃən kɒ́ntɛkst ənd rɪfájn ðɛm ówvər sɛ́vrəl tɜ́rnz. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw ǽd tə ðij éjdʒənt?
trans_Explanation: ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən túwl lɛ́ts ə mɒ́dəl ɪn ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API ɔr ə fáwndrij éjdʒənt krijéjt ɔr ɛ́dɪt ɪ́mɪdʒɪz æz pɑ́rt əv ə kɒ̀nvərséjʃən baj júwzɪŋ ə GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəl dɪplɔ́jmənt, sów ðə mɒ́dəl rájts ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ prɒ́mpt frəm kɒ́ntɛkst ənd rɛ́fɪnɪz ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ əkrɔ́s tɜ́rnz. ðə mɒ́dəl dɪsájdz wɛ́n tə kɔ́l ðə túwl, ənd áwtpʊ̀ts ərájv æz ɪ́mɪdʒ dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən kɔ́l ájtəmz ðæt kəntéjn base64 ɪ́mɪdʒ déjtə, wɪð ɒ́pʃənəl pɑ́rʃəl ɪ́mɪdʒɪz wɛ́n stríjmɪŋ. mə́ltij-tɜ́rn ɛ́dɪtɪŋ wɜ́rks baj rɛ́fɛrrɪŋ tə ɜ́rlijər ɪ́mɪdʒ áwtpʊ̀ts ɔr rɪspɒ́nsɪz rǽðər ðən rɛ́-ə́plowdɪŋ fájlz. fɔr stǽndəlòwn, sɪ́ŋɡəl-ʃɒ́t dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən wɪðáwt ə kɒ̀nvərséjʃən, kɔ́l ðij ɪ́mɪdʒɪz API dɪrɛ́ktlij.

Question: Which model in Foundry generates short videos with synchronized audio from text prompts or a reference image?
Explanation: Sora 2 is OpenAI's video generation model in Foundry (preview) that creates short videos from text prompts (text-to-video), from a reference image (image-to-video) and from an existing generated video (remix), and it generates synchronized audio, such as dialogue and sound effects, in the output. It is called through the Videos API at /openai/v1/videos with the OpenAI SDK (videos.create, videos.retrieve, videos.download_content and videos.remix). Key parameters are prompt, size (720x1280 portrait by default, or 1280x720 landscape), seconds (4, 8 or 12, default 4) and an optional input_reference image that must match the requested size. Prompts work best when they describe the shot type, subject, action, setting, lighting and camera motion.
trans_Question: wɪ́tʃ mɒ́dəl ɪn fáwndrij dʒɛ́nərèjts ʃɔ́rt vɪ́dijòwz wɪð sɪ́ŋkrənàjzd ɔ́dijòw frəm tɛ́kst prɒ́mpts ɔr ə rɛ́frəns ɪ́mɪdʒ?
trans_Explanation: sɔ́rə 2 ɪz ówpənAIz vɪ́dijòw dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən mɒ́dəl ɪn fáwndrij (príjvjuw) ðæt krijéjts ʃɔ́rt vɪ́dijòwz frəm tɛ́kst prɒ́mpts (tɛ́kst-tə-vɪ́dijòw), frəm ə rɛ́frəns ɪ́mɪdʒ (ɪ́mɪdʒ-tə-vɪ́dijòw) ənd frəm ən ɪɡzɪ́stɪŋ dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd vɪ́dijòw (ríjmɪks), ənd ɪt dʒɛ́nərèjts sɪ́ŋkrənàjzd ɔ́dijòw, sə́tʃ æz dájəlɔ̀ɡ ənd sáwnd ɪfɛ́kts, ɪn ðij áwtpʊ̀t. ɪt ɪz kɔ́ld θrúw ðə vɪ́dijòwz API ət /openai/v1/videos wɪð ðij ówpənAI SDK (videos.create, videos.retrieve, videos.download_content ənd videos.remix). kíj pərǽmətərz ɑr prɒ́mpt, sájz (720x1280 pɔ́rtrət baj dɪfɔ́lt, ɔr 1280x720 lǽndskèjp), sɛ́kəndz (4, 8 ɔr 12, dɪfɔ́lt 4) ənd ən ɒ́pʃənəl input_reference ɪ́mɪdʒ ðæt məst mǽtʃ ðə rɪkwɛ́stɪd sájz. prɒ́mpts wɜ́rk bɛ́st wɛ́n ðej dɪskrájb ðə ʃɒ́t tájp, sə́bdʒɛkt, ǽkʃən, sɛ́tɪŋ, lájtɪŋ ənd kǽmrəz mówʃən.

Question: After your app calls videos.create for Sora 2, the response doesn't contain the video. What must the app do next?
Explanation: Video generation is an asynchronous job: creating a video returns a job object with an ID and a status such as queued or in_progress, and the app polls (for example with videos.retrieve) until the status becomes completed or failed, then downloads the MP4 with videos.download_content. Failed jobs include a failure reason, such as a content policy violation, and webhook events (video.completed and video.failed) can replace polling where supported. Only a couple of generation jobs can run concurrently, and jobs are available for only 24 hours, so download and store results promptly. The first-generation Sora used a separate jobs API (/video/generations/jobs) with parameters such as n_seconds and n_variants.
trans_Question: ǽftər jɔr ǽp kɔ́lz videos.create fɔr sɔ́rə 2, ðə rɪspɒ́ns də́zənt kəntéjn ðə vɪ́dijòw. wɒ́t məst ðij ǽp dúw nɛ́kst?
trans_Explanation: vɪ́dijòw dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən ɪz ən ejsɪ́ŋkrənəs dʒɒ́b: krijéjtɪŋ ə vɪ́dijòw rɪtɜ́rnz ə dʒɒ́b ɒ́bdʒɛkt wɪð ən ID ənd ə stéjtəs sə́tʃ æz kjúwd ɔr in_progress, ənd ðij ǽp pówlz (fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl wɪð videos.retrieve) əntɪ́l ðə stéjtəs bɪkə́mz kəmplíjtɪd ɔr féjld, ðɛ́n dáwnlowds ðə MP4 wɪð videos.download_content. féjld dʒɒ́bz ɪnklúwd ə féjljər ríjzən, sə́tʃ æz ə kɒ́ntɛnt pɒ́lɪsij vàjəléjʃən, ənd wɛ́bhʊ̀k ɪvɛ́nts (video.completed ənd video.failed) kən rɪpléjs pówlɪŋ wɛ́r səpɔ́rtɪd. ównlij ə kə́pəl əv dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən dʒɒ́bz kən rə́n kənkɜ́rəntlij, ənd dʒɒ́bz ɑr əvéjləbəl fɔr ównlij 24 áwərz, sów dàwnlówd ənd stɔ́r rɪzə́lts prɒ́mptlij. ðə fɪ́rst-dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən sɔ́rə júwzd ə sɛ́prət dʒɒ́bz API (/video/generations/jobs) wɪð pərǽmətərz sə́tʃ æz n_seconds ənd n_variants.

Question: A Sora 2 image-to-video request is rejected because of its reference image. Which kind of input image is currently rejected?
Explanation: Sora 2 content restrictions in Foundry limit what can be generated or used as input: input images that contain human faces are currently rejected, real people (including public figures) can't be generated, copyrighted characters and copyrighted music are rejected, and output is limited to content suitable for audiences under 18. Prompts and outputs also pass through content filtering, and a blocked request returns no video together with a failure reason. The reference image must be JPEG, PNG or WebP and match the requested video size exactly. Knowing these limits helps you design prompts and inputs that won't be rejected.
trans_Question: ə sɔ́rə 2 ɪ́mɪdʒ-tə-vɪ́dijòw rɪkwɛ́st ɪz rɪdʒɛ́ktɪd bɪkɒ́z əv ɪts rɛ́frəns ɪ́mɪdʒ. wɪ́tʃ kájnd əv ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒ ɪz kɜ́rəntlij rɪdʒɛ́ktɪd?
trans_Explanation: sɔ́rə 2 kɒ́ntɛnt rɪstrɪ́kʃənz ɪn fáwndrij lɪ́mɪt wɒ́t kən bij dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd ɔr júwzd æz ɪ́npʊ̀t: ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ðæt kəntéjn hjúwmən féjsɪz ɑr kɜ́rəntlij rɪdʒɛ́ktɪd, ríjəl píjpəl (ɪnklúwdɪŋ pə́blɪk fɪ́ɡjərz) kǽnt bij dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd, kɒ́pijràjtɪd kǽrəktərz ənd kɒ́pijràjtɪd mjúwzɪk ɑr rɪdʒɛ́ktɪd, ənd áwtpʊ̀t ɪz lɪ́mɪtɪd tə kɒ́ntɛnt súwtəbəl fɔr ɔ́dijənsɪz ə́ndər 18. prɒ́mpts ənd áwtpʊ̀ts ɔ́lsow pǽs θrúw kɒ́ntɛnt fɪ́ltərɪŋ, ənd ə blɒ́kt rɪkwɛ́st rɪtɜ́rnz nów vɪ́dijòw təɡɛ́ðər wɪð ə féjljər ríjzən. ðə rɛ́frəns ɪ́mɪdʒ məst bij JPEG, PNG ɔr wɛ́bP ənd mǽtʃ ðə rɪkwɛ́stɪd vɪ́dijòw sájz ɪɡzǽktlij. nówɪŋ ðijz lɪ́mɪts hɛ́lps juw dɪzájn prɒ́mpts ənd ɪ́npʊ̀ts ðæt wɒ́nt bij rɪdʒɛ́ktɪd.

Question: You need to replace only the sky in a product photo and leave everything else unchanged by using images.edit. What must you supply along with the image and prompt?
Explanation: Inpainting is mask-based image editing in which a mask marks the region to change and the model regenerates only that area according to the prompt, keeping the rest of the image. With GPT-image models, the mask is a PNG with the same dimensions as the input image, and fully transparent pixels (alpha of zero) mark the area to edit. The Image Edit API takes multipart form data with up to 16 input images (PNG or JPG, each under 50 MB), and when several images are supplied, the mask applies to the first image. Without a mask, edits are prompt-driven and the model may change any part of the image.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə rɪpléjs ównlij ðə skáj ɪn ə prɒ́dəkt fówtòw ənd líjv ɛ́vrɪθɪ̀ŋ ɛ́ls ə̀ntʃéjndʒd baj júwzɪŋ images.edit. wɒ́t məst juw səpláj əlɔ́ŋ wɪð ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ ənd prɒ́mpt?
trans_Explanation: ɪnpéjntɪŋ ɪz mǽsk-béjst ɪ́mɪdʒ ɛ́dɪtɪŋ ɪn wɪ́tʃ ə mǽsk mɑ́rks ðə ríjdʒən tə tʃéjndʒ ənd ðə mɒ́dəl rɛ́dʒɛnɛrætɪz ównlij ðæt ɛ́rijə əkɔ́rdɪŋ tə ðə prɒ́mpt, kíjpɪŋ ðə rɛ́st əv ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ. wɪð GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz, ðə mǽsk ɪz ə PNG wɪð ðə séjm dɪmɛ́nʃənz æz ðij ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒ, ənd fʊ́lij trænsprɛ́rənt pɪ́ksəlz (ǽlfæ əv zɪ́row) mɑ́rk ðij ɛ́rijə tə ɛ́dɪt. ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ ɛ́dɪt API téjks mə́ltɪpært fɔ́rm déjtə wɪð ə́p tə 16 ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒɪz (PNG ɔr JPG, íjtʃ ə́ndər 50 MB), ənd wɛ́n sɛ́vrəl ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ɑr səplájd, ðə mǽsk əplájz tə ðə fɜ́rst ɪ́mɪdʒ. wɪðáwt ə mǽsk, ɛ́dɪts ɑr prɒ́mpt-drɪ́vən ənd ðə mɒ́dəl mej tʃéjndʒ ɛ́nij pɑ́rt əv ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ.

Question: Image edits keep altering a person's facial features and the exact style of a logo from the input image. Which parameter should you set to high?
Explanation: The input_fidelity parameter controls how much effort an image edit puts into preserving the style and features of the input images, especially faces and logos: high keeps fine details closer to the originals, and low (the default) allows more freedom. It applies to the edit endpoint with supported GPT-image models but isn't available for gpt-image-1-mini, and high fidelity increases processing and token cost. Edits can combine several reference images, for example placing a product from one photo into a scene from another, with the prompt describing how to compose them. For repeatable brand assets, combine high input fidelity with explicit prompt constraints about what must not change.
trans_Question: ɪ́mɪdʒ ɛ́dɪts kíjp ɔ́ltərɪŋ ə pɜ́rsənz féjʃəl fíjtʃərz ənd ðij ɪɡzǽkt stájl əv ə lówɡow frəm ðij ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒ. wɪ́tʃ pərǽmətər ʃʊd juw sɛ́t tə háj?
trans_Explanation: ðə input_fidelity pərǽmətər kəntrówlz háw mə́tʃ ɛ́fərt ən ɪ́mɪdʒ ɛ́dɪt pʊ́ts ɪ́ntə prɪzɜ́rvɪŋ ðə stájl ənd fíjtʃərz əv ðij ɪ́npʊ̀t ɪ́mɪdʒɪz, ɪspɛ́ʃəlij féjsɪz ənd lɒ́ɡɒs: háj kíjps fájn dɪtéjlz klówsər tə ðij ɒ́rɪdʒɪnæls, ənd lów (ðə dɪfɔ́lt) əláwz mɔ́r fríjdəm. ɪt əplájz tə ðij ɛ́dɪt ɪ́ndpɔ̀jnt wɪð səpɔ́rtɪd GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz bət ɪ́zənt əvéjləbəl fɔr gpt-image-1-mini, ənd háj fɪdɛ́lətij ɪnkríjsɪz prɒ́sɛsɪŋ ənd tówkən kɔ́st. ɛ́dɪts kən kɒ́mbajn sɛ́vrəl rɛ́frəns ɪ́mɪdʒɪz, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl pléjsɪŋ ə prɒ́dəkt frəm wə́n fówtòw ɪ́ntə ə síjn frəm ənə́ðər, wɪð ðə prɒ́mpt dɪskrájbɪŋ háw tə kɒ́mpɒs ðɛm. fɔr rɪpíjtəbəl brǽnd ǽsɛts, kɒ́mbajn háj ɪ́npʊ̀t fɪdɛ́lətij wɪð ɪksplɪ́sɪt prɒ́mpt kənstréjnts əbáwt wɒ́t məst nɒ́t tʃéjndʒ.

Question: A generated Sora 2 video is good, except the car should be red instead of blue. You want a targeted change without regenerating from scratch. What should you do?
Explanation: Video remix is a Sora 2 capability that creates a new video from an existing completed video by applying a targeted change described in a new prompt, such as a different color, lighting or setting, while preserving the original's structure, motion and composition. You call the remix operation with the source video ID (for example videos.remix with a video_ ID), and the result is a new video with its own ID, so you can iterate through a chain of versions. Small, single changes per remix give the most predictable results, while large changes work better as a new generation. Each remix is a new asynchronous job that must be polled and downloaded like any other video.
trans_Question: ə dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd sɔ́rə 2 vɪ́dijòw ɪz ɡʊ́d, ɪksɛ́pt ðə kɑ́r ʃʊd bij rɛ́d ɪnstɛ́d əv blúw. juw wɒ́nt ə tɑ́rɡətɪd tʃéjndʒ wɪðáwt rɛ́dʒɛnɛrætɪŋ frəm skrǽtʃ. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw dúw?
trans_Explanation: vɪ́dijòw ríjmɪks ɪz ə sɔ́rə 2 kèjpəbɪ́lɪtij ðæt krijéjts ə núw vɪ́dijòw frəm ən ɪɡzɪ́stɪŋ kəmplíjtɪd vɪ́dijòw baj əplájɪŋ ə tɑ́rɡətɪd tʃéjndʒ dɪskrájbd ɪn ə núw prɒ́mpt, sə́tʃ æz ə dɪ́frənt kə́lər, lájtɪŋ ɔr sɛ́tɪŋ, wájl prɪzɜ́rvɪŋ ðij ɒ́rɪdʒɪnæls strə́ktʃər, mówʃən ənd kɒ̀mpəzɪ́ʃən. juw kɔ́l ðə ríjmɪks ɒ̀pəréjʃən wɪð ðə sɔ́rs vɪ́dijòw ID (fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl videos.remix wɪð ə vɪ́dijòw_ ID), ənd ðə rɪzə́lt ɪz ə núw vɪ́dijòw wɪð ɪts ówn ID, sów juw kən ɪ́tə̀rèjt θrúw ə tʃéjn əv vɜ́rʒənz. smɔ́l, sɪ́ŋɡəl tʃéjndʒɪz pə́r ríjmɪks ɡɪ́v ðə mówst prɪdɪ́ktəbəl rɪzə́lts, wájl lɑ́rdʒ tʃéjndʒɪz wɜ́rk bɛ́tər æz ə núw dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən. íjtʃ ríjmɪks ɪz ə núw ejsɪ́ŋkrənəs dʒɒ́b ðæt məst bij pówld ənd dáwnlòwdɪd lájk ɛ́nij ə́ðər vɪ́dijòw.

Question: Your team edits generated videos over several days, but remix calls fail for videos created earlier in the week. What is the most likely cause?
Explanation: Generated video retention in Foundry is short: Sora jobs and their outputs are available for up to 24 hours after creation, after which they can't be retrieved, downloaded or used as a remix source, and the video must be generated again. An iterative video editing workflow should therefore download each completed video promptly to your own storage, such as Azure Blob Storage, and record its lineage: the parent video ID, the new video ID, the prompt and the settings used. Tracking lineage lets users compare versions, roll back to an earlier version and reproduce results. Plan remix steps within the retention window or regenerate from stored prompts when needed.
trans_Question: jɔr tíjm ɛ́dɪts dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd vɪ́dijòwz ówvər sɛ́vrəl déjz, bət ríjmɪks kɔ́lz féjl fɔr vɪ́dijòwz krijéjtɪd ɜ́rlijər ɪn ðə wíjk. wɒ́t ɪz ðə mówst lájklij kɔ́z?
trans_Explanation: dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd vɪ́dijòw rɪtɛ́nʃən ɪn fáwndrij ɪz ʃɔ́rt: sɔ́rə dʒɒ́bz ənd ðɛr áwtpʊ̀ts ɑr əvéjləbəl fɔr ə́p tə 24 áwərz ǽftər krijéjʃən, ǽftər wɪ́tʃ ðej kǽnt bij rɪtríjvd, dáwnlòwdɪd ɔr júwzd æz ə ríjmɪks sɔ́rs, ənd ðə vɪ́dijòw məst bij dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd əɡɛ́n. ən ɪ́tərèjtɪv vɪ́dijòw ɛ́dɪtɪŋ wɜ́rkflòw ʃʊd ðɛ́rfɔ̀r dàwnlówd íjtʃ kəmplíjtɪd vɪ́dijòw prɒ́mptlij tə jɔr ówn stɔ́rɪdʒ, sə́tʃ æz ǽʒər blɒ́b stɔ́rɪdʒ, ənd rɛ́kərd ɪts lɪ́nijɪdʒ: ðə pɛ́rənt vɪ́dijòw ID, ðə núw vɪ́dijòw ID, ðə prɒ́mpt ənd ðə sɛ́tɪŋz júwzd. trǽkɪŋ lɪ́nijɪdʒ lɛ́ts júwzərz kəmpɛ́r vɜ́rʒənz, rówl bǽk tə ən ɜ́rlijər vɜ́rʒən ənd rìjprədúws rɪzə́lts. plǽn ríjmɪks stɛ́ps wɪðɪ́n ðə rɪtɛ́nʃən wɪ́ndow ɔr rijdʒɛ́nərèjt frəm stɔ́rd prɒ́mpts wɛ́n níjdɪd.

Question: You need product images with transparent backgrounds for a web store from a GPT-image model. Which settings should you use?
Explanation: Image output controls for GPT-image models include size, quality, n, output_format, output_compression and background. A transparent background requires background set to transparent together with output_format PNG, because JPEG doesn't support transparency, and the default background is auto. On Azure, output_format supports PNG (the default) and JPEG, and output_compression (0 to 100, default 100) reduces file size for compressed formats. Transparency works best with simple subjects such as products, logos or stickers, and medium or high quality gives cleaner edges.
trans_Question: juw níjd prɒ́dəkt ɪ́mɪdʒɪz wɪð trænsprɛ́rənt bǽkɡràwndz fɔr ə wɛ́b stɔ́r frəm ə GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəl. wɪ́tʃ sɛ́tɪŋz ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: ɪ́mɪdʒ áwtpʊ̀t kəntrówlz fɔr GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz ɪnklúwd sájz, kwɑ́lɪtij, n, output_format, output_compression ənd bǽkɡràwnd. ə trænsprɛ́rənt bǽkɡràwnd rɪkwájərz bǽkɡràwnd sɛ́t tə trænsprɛ́rənt təɡɛ́ðər wɪð output_format PNG, bɪkɒ́z JPEG də́zənt səpɔ́rt trænspɛ́rənsij, ənd ðə dɪfɔ́lt bǽkɡràwnd ɪz ɔ́tow. ɒn ǽʒər, output_format səpɔ́rts PNG (ðə dɪfɔ́lt) ənd JPEG, ənd output_compression (0 tə 100, dɪfɔ́lt 100) rɪdúwsɪz fájl sájz fɔr kɒ́mprɛssɪd fɔ́rmæ̀ts. trænspɛ́rənsij wɜ́rks bɛ́st wɪð sɪ́mpəl sə́bdʒɪkts sə́tʃ æz prɒ́dəkts, lɒ́ɡɒs ɔr stɪ́kɛrs, ənd míjdijəm ɔr háj kwɑ́lɪtij ɡɪ́vz klɛ́nɛr ɛ́dʒɪz.

Question: You need many quick, low-cost draft images for internal brainstorming from a GPT-image model. Which setting should you change?
Explanation: The quality parameter of GPT-image models (low, medium or high, with high as the default for most models on Azure) trades rendering detail against speed and cost, because higher quality generates more image output tokens. Low quality suits drafts, thumbnails and rapid iteration, while high quality suits final assets with fine detail and text. Size also drives cost: GPT-image-1 series models support 1024x1024, 1024x1536 and 1536x1024, and gpt-image-2 supports flexible sizes within pixel and aspect ratio limits. Image deployments have low default rate limits (about five images per minute), so plan draft volumes accordingly.
trans_Question: juw níjd mɛ́nij kwɪ́k, lów-kɔ́st drǽft ɪ́mɪdʒɪz fɔr ɪntɜ́rnəl bréjnstɔ̀rmɪŋ frəm ə GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəl. wɪ́tʃ sɛ́tɪŋ ʃʊd juw tʃéjndʒ?
trans_Explanation: ðə kwɑ́lɪtij pərǽmətər əv GPT-ɪ́mɪdʒ mɒ́dəlz (lów, míjdijəm ɔr háj, wɪð háj æz ðə dɪfɔ́lt fɔr mówst mɒ́dəlz ɒn ǽʒər) tréjdz rɛ́ndərɪŋ díjtèjl əɡɛ́nst spíjd ənd kɔ́st, bɪkɒ́z hájər kwɑ́lɪtij dʒɛ́nərèjts mɔ́r ɪ́mɪdʒ áwtpʊ̀t tówkənz. lów kwɑ́lɪtij súwts drǽfts, θə́mnèjlz ənd rǽpɪd ɪ̀təréjʃən, wájl háj kwɑ́lɪtij súwts fájnəl ǽsɛts wɪð fájn díjtèjl ənd tɛ́kst. sájz ɔ́lsow drájvz kɔ́st: GPT-image-1 sɪ́rijz mɒ́dəlz səpɔ́rt 1024x1024, 1024x1536 ənd 1536x1024, ənd gpt-image-2 səpɔ́rts flɛ́ksɪbəl sájzɪz wɪðɪ́n pɪ́ksɛl ənd ǽspɛkt réjʃijòw lɪ́mɪts. ɪ́mɪdʒ dɪplɔ́jmənts həv lów dɪfɔ́lt réjt lɪ́mɪts (əbáwt fájv ɪ́mɪdʒɪz pə́r mɪ́nət), sów plǽn drǽft vɒ́ljuwmz əkɔ́rdɪŋlij.

Question: You need a 12-second landscape video from Sora 2. Which parameter values should you set?
Explanation: Video generation controls for Sora 2 include seconds, the clip duration (4, 8 or 12 seconds, default 4), and size, the resolution and aspect ratio (720x1280 portrait, the default, or 1280x720 landscape). Longer and higher-resolution videos take longer to generate and cost more, and an input_reference image must match the chosen size. The first-generation Sora used width, height, n_seconds and n_variants (several variations per job, fewer at higher resolutions). Use the shortest duration that meets the need while iterating, then generate the final version.

trans_Explanation: vɪ́dijòw dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən kəntrówlz fɔr sɔ́rə 2 ɪnklúwd sɛ́kəndz, ðə klɪ́p dʊréjʃən (4, 8 ɔr 12 sɛ́kəndz, dɪfɔ́lt 4), ənd sájz, ðə rɛ̀zəlúwʃən ənd ǽspɛkt réjʃijòw (720x1280 pɔ́rtrət, ðə dɪfɔ́lt, ɔr 1280x720 lǽndskèjp). lɔ́ŋɡər ənd hájər-rɛ̀zəlúwʃən vɪ́dijòwz téjk lɔ́ŋɡər tə dʒɛ́nərèjt ənd kɔ́st mɔ́r, ənd ən input_reference ɪ́mɪdʒ məst mǽtʃ ðə tʃówzən sájz. ðə fɪ́rst-dʒɛ̀nəréjʃən sɔ́rə júwzd wɪ́dθ, hájt, n_seconds ənd n_variants (sɛ́vrəl vɛ̀rijéjʃənz pə́r dʒɒ́b, fjúwər ət hájər rɛ̀zəlúwʃənz). júws ðə ʃɔ́rtəst dʊréjʃən ðæt míjts ðə níjd wájl ɪ́tɛrætɪŋ, ðɛ́n dʒɛ́nərèjt ðə fájnəl vɜ́rʒən.

Question: You need to send a local image file to a vision-enabled model in a chat request without hosting the image anywhere. What should you include in the message?
Explanation: Multimodal prompts combine text and images in one request: in Chat Completions an image is an image_url content part, and in the Responses API it is an input_image item, and either can hold a public HTTPS URL or a base64 data URL (data:image/png;base64,...). Data URLs suit local or private images because the service can't fetch files from your machine or private network, while URLs avoid large payloads. Vision-enabled models such as GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5 and Phi-4-multimodal accept common formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP and non-animated GIF) and several images per request within size limits. In the Responses API you can also upload an image with the Files API and reference it by file ID.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə sɛ́nd ə lówkəl ɪ́mɪdʒ fájl tə ə vɪ́ʒən-ɪnéjbəld mɒ́dəl ɪn ə tʃǽt rɪkwɛ́st wɪðáwt hówstɪŋ ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ ɛ́nijwɛ̀r. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw ɪnklúwd ɪn ðə mɛ́sɪdʒ?
trans_Explanation: mə̀ltijmówdəl prɒ́mpts kɒ́mbajn tɛ́kst ənd ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ɪn wə́n rɪkwɛ́st: ɪn tʃǽt kəmplíjʃənz ən ɪ́mɪdʒ ɪz ən image_url kɒ́ntɛnt pɑ́rt, ənd ɪn ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API ɪt ɪz ən input_image ájtəm, ənd íjðər kən hówld ə pə́blɪk HTTPS URL ɔr ə base64 déjtə URL (data:image/png;base64,...). déjtə URLz súwt lówkəl ɔr prájvət ɪ́mɪdʒɪz bɪkɒ́z ðə sɜ́rvɪs kǽnt fɛ́tʃ fájlz frəm jɔr məʃíjn ɔr prájvət nɛ́twɜ̀rk, wájl URLz əvɔ́jd lɑ́rdʒ péjlòwdz. vɪ́ʒən-ɪnéjbəld mɒ́dəlz sə́tʃ æz GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5 ənd Phi-4-multimodal əksɛ́pt kɒ́mən fɔ́rmæ̀ts (JPEG, PNG, wɛ́bP ənd nɒ́n-ǽnɪmèjtɪd GIF) ənd sɛ́vrəl ɪ́mɪdʒɪz pə́r rɪkwɛ́st wɪðɪ́n sájz lɪ́mɪts. ɪn ðə rɪspɒ́nsɪz API juw kən ɔ́lsow əplówd ən ɪ́mɪdʒ wɪð ðə fájlz API ənd rɛ́frəns ɪt baj fájl ID.

Question: Your app sends thousands of images to a vision model only to identify the overall scene type, and image token costs are high. What should you set?
Explanation: The image detail parameter (low, high or auto) controls how a vision model processes an image and how many input tokens it costs. Low detail analyzes a downscaled version (512 x 512 pixels) for a small, fixed token cost (85 tokens on GPT-4o), which is enough for overall scene, color or layout questions, while high detail also analyzes detailed tiles, costing more tokens but capturing small text and fine features. Auto lets the model choose based on the image size. Image tokens count toward the context window, rate limits and cost, so resizing images and choosing the right detail level are key optimizations.

Question: A model must compare before and after maintenance photos of the same machine part and describe the differences. How should you send the photos?
Explanation: Multi-image prompts let a vision-enabled model reason across several images in a single request, for example to compare before and after photos, check a product against a reference image or read a multipage form, because all images share one context. Each image is a separate content part, and the prompt should say how the images relate, for example by labeling them Image 1 and Image 2, and what to compare. Every image adds input tokens, so use low detail where fine detail isn't needed. For precise pixel-level differences, combine the model with deterministic image processing or object detection, because LLMs can miss very small changes.
trans_Question: ə mɒ́dəl məst kəmpɛ́r bɪfɔ́r ənd ǽftər méjntnəns fówtòwz əv ðə séjm məʃíjn pɑ́rt ənd dɪskrájb ðə dɪ́frənsɪz. háw ʃʊd juw sɛ́nd ðə fówtòwz?
trans_Explanation: mə́ltij-ɪ́mɪdʒ prɒ́mpts lɛ́t ə vɪ́ʒən-ɪnéjbəld mɒ́dəl ríjzən əkrɔ́s sɛ́vrəl ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ɪn ə sɪ́ŋɡəl rɪkwɛ́st, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl tə kəmpɛ́r bɪfɔ́r ənd ǽftər fówtòwz, tʃɛ́k ə prɒ́dəkt əɡɛ́nst ə rɛ́frəns ɪ́mɪdʒ ɔr ríjd ə mə́ltɪpædʒ fɔ́rm, bɪkɒ́z ɔ́l ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ʃɛ́r wə́n kɒ́ntɛkst. íjtʃ ɪ́mɪdʒ ɪz ə sɛ́prət kɒ́ntɛnt pɑ́rt, ənd ðə prɒ́mpt ʃʊd séj háw ðij ɪ́mɪdʒɪz rɪléjt, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl baj léjblɪŋ ðɛm ɪ́mɪdʒ 1 ənd ɪ́mɪdʒ 2, ənd wɒ́t tə kəmpɛ́r. ɛ́vrij ɪ́mɪdʒ ǽdz ɪ́npʊ̀t tówkənz, sów júws lów díjtèjl wɛ́r fájn díjtèjl ɪ́zənt níjdɪd. fɔr prɪsájs pɪ́ksɛl-lɛ́vəl dɪ́frənsɪz, kɒ́mbajn ðə mɒ́dəl wɪð dɪtɜ̀rmɪnɪ́stɪk ɪ́mɪdʒ prɒ́sɛsɪŋ ɔr ɒ́bdʒɛkt dɪtɛ́kʃən, bɪkɒ́z LLMz kən mɪ́s vɛ́rij smɔ́l tʃéjndʒɪz.

Question: An image library needs a one-sentence caption for search results and a detailed paragraph for the detail page, from one vision model call per image. What should you request?
Explanation: Image captioning with multimodal models is controlled mainly through the prompt: specify the length (for example one sentence of under 20 words versus a detailed paragraph), the focus (objects, actions, setting, visible text, mood), the audience and the style, and tell the model not to guess unseen details. Requesting a structured output, such as JSON with short_caption and detailed_description fields enforced by a JSON Schema, produces both caption types in one call and makes results easy to store and index. For large collections, process images in parallel or with batch processing, keeping one image per request when captions must be independent. Consistent caption styles across a library also improve search relevance.
trans_Question: ən ɪ́mɪdʒ lájbrɛ̀rij níjdz ə wə́n-sɛ́ntəns kǽpʃən fɔr sɜ́rtʃ rɪzə́lts ənd ə dɪtéjld pǽrəɡræ̀f fɔr ðə díjtèjl péjdʒ, frəm wə́n vɪ́ʒən mɒ́dəl kɔ́l pə́r ɪ́mɪdʒ. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw rɪkwɛ́st?
trans_Explanation: ɪ́mɪdʒ kǽpʃənɪŋ wɪð mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəlz ɪz kəntrówld méjnlij θrúw ðə prɒ́mpt: spɛ́sɪfàj ðə lɛ́ŋθ (fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl wə́n sɛ́ntəns əv ə́ndər 20 wɜ́rdz vɜ́rsəs ə dɪtéjld pǽrəɡræ̀f), ðə fówkəs (ɒ́bdʒɛkts, ǽkʃənz, sɛ́tɪŋ, vɪ́zɪbəl tɛ́kst, múwd), ðij ɔ́dijəns ənd ðə stájl, ənd tɛ́l ðə mɒ́dəl nɒ́t tə ɡə́ɛss ə́nsijn dɪtéjlz. rɪkwɛ́stɪŋ ə strə́ktʃərd áwtpʊ̀t, sə́tʃ æz JSON wɪð short_caption ənd detailed_description fíjldz ɪnfɔ́rst baj ə JSON skíjmə, prədúwsɪz bówθ kǽpʃən tájps ɪn wə́n kɔ́l ənd méjks rɪzə́lts íjzij tə stɔ́r ənd ɪ́ndɛks. fɔr lɑ́rdʒ kəlɛ́kʃənz, prɒ́sɛs ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ɪn pǽrəlɛ̀l ɔr wɪð bǽtʃ prɒ́sɛsɪŋ, kíjpɪŋ wə́n ɪ́mɪdʒ pə́r rɪkwɛ́st wɛ́n kǽpʃənz məst bij ɪ̀ndɪpɛ́ndənt. kənsɪ́stənt kǽpʃən stájlz əkrɔ́s ə lájbrɛ̀rij ɔ́lsow ɪmprúwv sɜ́rtʃ rɛ́lɪvəns.

Question: You need separate captions for individual regions of an image, such as 'a red car on the left' and 'a man holding an umbrella', each with its location. What should you generate?
Explanation: Dense captions are captions generated for multiple regions of an image, each describing a detected object or area together with its bounding box, rather than one caption for the whole image. Azure AI Vision Image Analysis 4.0 offers dense captions (up to 10 regions) alongside caption, tags, objects, people, smart crops and read (OCR) features, although Image Analysis is scheduled for retirement in September 2028, and multimodal models or Content Understanding are the recommended paths for new solutions. With a multimodal model, you can ask for region-by-region descriptions in structured JSON, but its location estimates are approximate. Dense captions support detailed search indexing, accessibility descriptions and visual question answering.
trans_Question: juw níjd sɛ́prət kǽpʃənz fɔr ɪ̀ndɪvɪ́dʒuwəl ríjdʒənz əv ən ɪ́mɪdʒ, sə́tʃ æz 'ə rɛ́d kɑ́r ɒn ðə lɛ́ft' ənd 'ə mǽn hówldɪŋ ən əmbrɛ́lə', íjtʃ wɪð ɪts lowkéjʃən. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw dʒɛ́nərèjt?
trans_Explanation: dɛ́ns kǽpʃənz ɑr kǽpʃənz dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd fɔr mə́ltɪpəl ríjdʒənz əv ən ɪ́mɪdʒ, íjtʃ dɪskrájbɪŋ ə dɪtɛ́ktɪd ɒ́bdʒɛkt ɔr ɛ́rijə təɡɛ́ðər wɪð ɪts báwndɪŋ bɒ́ks, rǽðər ðən wə́n kǽpʃən fɔr ðə hówl ɪ́mɪdʒ. ǽʒər AI vɪ́ʒən ɪ́mɪdʒ ənǽlɪsɪs 4.0 ɔ́fərz dɛ́ns kǽpʃənz (ə́p tə 10 ríjdʒənz) əlɔ̀ŋsájd kǽpʃən, tǽɡz, ɒ́bdʒɛkts, píjpəl, smɑ́rt krɒ́ps ənd ríjd (OCR) fíjtʃərz, ɔ̀lðów ɪ́mɪdʒ ənǽlɪsɪs ɪz skɛ́dʒuwld fɔr rɪtájərmənt ɪn sɛptɛ́mbər 2028, ənd mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəlz ɔr kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ ɑr ðə rɛ̀kəmɛ́ndɪd pǽðz fɔr núw səlúwʃənz. wɪð ə mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəl, juw kən ǽsk fɔr ríjdʒən-baj-ríjdʒən dɪskrɪ́pʃənz ɪn strə́ktʃərd JSON, bət ɪts lowkéjʃən ɛ́stɪməts ɑr əprɒ́ksɪmət. dɛ́ns kǽpʃənz səpɔ́rt dɪtéjld sɜ́rtʃ ɪ́ndɛksɪŋ, əksɛ̀sɪbɪ́lɪtij dɪskrɪ́pʃənz ənd vɪ́ʒwəl kwɛ́stʃən ǽnsərɪŋ.

Question: A support app answers questions about photos of dashboards and error screens. What should the system prompt require so that answers are grounded in the image?
Explanation: Visual question answering (VQA) is answering natural language questions about an image, such as reading values from a chart, dashboard or form, and grounded VQA requires answers to be based only on what is visible. Prompts should tell the model to cite the visual evidence it used (for example the label, region or text it read), to say when the information isn't visible or is unreadable instead of guessing, and to separate observations from inferences. Charts, tables and screenshots benefit from high image detail, and OCR text extracted by a document or vision service can be added as extra grounding. Evaluate VQA answers against ground truth, because multimodal models can still misread small text or numbers.
trans_Question: ə səpɔ́rt ǽp ǽnsərz kwɛ́stʃənz əbáwt fówtòwz əv dǽʃbɔ̀rdz ənd ɛ́rər skríjnz. wɒ́t ʃʊd ðə sɪ́stəm prɒ́mpt rɪkwájər sów ðæt ǽnsərz ɑr ɡráwndɪd ɪn ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ?
trans_Explanation: vɪ́ʒwəl kwɛ́stʃən ǽnsərɪŋ (VQA) ɪz ǽnsərɪŋ nǽtʃərəl lǽŋɡwɪdʒ kwɛ́stʃənz əbáwt ən ɪ́mɪdʒ, sə́tʃ æz ríjdɪŋ vǽljuwz frəm ə tʃɑ́rt, dǽʃbɔ̀rd ɔr fɔ́rm, ənd ɡráwndɪd VQA rɪkwájərz ǽnsərz tə bij béjst ównlij ɒn wɒ́t ɪz vɪ́zɪbəl. prɒ́mpts ʃʊd tɛ́l ðə mɒ́dəl tə sájt ðə vɪ́ʒwəl ɛ́vɪdəns ɪt júwzd (fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl ðə léjbəl, ríjdʒən ɔr tɛ́kst ɪt ríjd), tə séj wɛ́n ðij ɪ̀nfərméjʃən ɪ́zənt vɪ́zɪbəl ɔr ɪz ə́nrɛdəbəl ɪnstɛ́d əv ɡɛ́sɪŋ, ənd tə sɛ́prət ɒ̀bzərvéjʃənz frəm ɪ́nfɛrɛnkɪz. tʃɑ́rts, téjbəlz ənd skríjnʃɒ̀ts bɛ́nɪfɪt frəm háj ɪ́mɪdʒ díjtèjl, ənd OCR tɛ́kst ɪkstrǽktɪd baj ə dɒ́kjəmənt ɔr vɪ́ʒən sɜ́rvɪs kən bij ǽdɪd æz ɛ́kstrə ɡráwndɪŋ. ɪvǽljuwèjt VQA ǽnsərz əɡɛ́nst ɡráwnd trúwθ, bɪkɒ́z mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəlz kən stɪ́l mɪ̀srɛ́d smɔ́l tɛ́kst ɔr nə́mbərz.

Question: Answers about a scanned financial table must exactly match the printed numbers, but the vision model sometimes misreads digits. What should you add?
Explanation: OCR grounding means extracting the text and table structure from an image with a dedicated service, such as Content Understanding or Document Intelligence layout, and passing it to the multimodal model together with the image, so answers rely on exactly recognized text rather than the model's visual reading alone. This reduces misread digits and improves accuracy for tables, forms, receipts and dense documents, and the extracted coordinates can link answers back to regions of the page. Use high image detail when the model must still interpret layout or visual elements. For numeric answers, add validation in code, for example checking that totals equal the sum of their items.
trans_Question: ǽnsərz əbáwt ə skǽnd fájnæ̀nʃəl téjbəl məst ɪɡzǽktlij mǽtʃ ðə prɪ́ntɪd nə́mbərz, bət ðə vɪ́ʒən mɒ́dəl sə́mtàjmz mɪ̀sríjdz dɪ́dʒɪts. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw ǽd?
trans_Explanation: OCR ɡráwndɪŋ míjnz ɪkstrǽktɪŋ ðə tɛ́kst ənd téjbəl strə́ktʃər frəm ən ɪ́mɪdʒ wɪð ə dɛ́dɪkèjtɪd sɜ́rvɪs, sə́tʃ æz kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ ɔr dɒ́kjəmənt ɪntɛ́lɪdʒəns léjàwt, ənd pǽsɪŋ ɪt tə ðə mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəl təɡɛ́ðər wɪð ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ, sów ǽnsərz rɪláj ɒn ɪɡzǽktlij rɛ́kəɡnàjzd tɛ́kst rǽðər ðən ðə mɒ́dəlz vɪ́ʒwəl ríjdɪŋ əlówn. ðɪs rɪdúwsɪz mɪ̀srɛ́d dɪ́dʒɪts ənd ɪ̀mprúwvz ǽkjərəsij fɔr téjbəlz, fɔ́rmz, rɪsíjts ənd dɛ́ns dɒ́kjəmənts, ənd ðij ɪkstrǽktɪd kowɔ́rdɪnèjts kən lɪ́ŋk ǽnsərz bǽk tə ríjdʒənz əv ðə péjdʒ. júws háj ɪ́mɪdʒ díjtèjl wɛ́n ðə mɒ́dəl məst stɪ́l ɪntɜ́rprət léjàwt ɔr vɪ́ʒwəl ɛ́ləmənts. fɔr nuwmɛ́rɪk ǽnsərz, ǽd væ̀lɪdéjʃən ɪn kówd, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl tʃɛ́kɪŋ ðæt tówtəlz íjkwəl ðə sə́m əv ðɛr ájtəmz.

Question: You need alt text for informative product images on a website that must meet WCAG. What should the generated alt text be?
Explanation: Alt text (alternative text) is a short text equivalent of an image that screen readers announce, and WCAG success criterion 1.1.1 (Non-text Content) requires it for informative images. Good alt text conveys the image's purpose and key content in context, usually in a sentence or less (a common guideline is under about 125 characters), and avoids redundant phrases such as 'image of' or keyword stuffing. Decorative images that add no information should have an empty alt attribute so screen readers skip them. When generating alt text with a multimodal model, give it the page context and audience, and have people review images where accuracy matters.
trans_Question: juw níjd ɒ́lt tɛ́kst fɔr ɪnfɔ́rmətɪv prɒ́dəkt ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ɒn ə wɛ́bsàjt ðæt məst míjt WCAG. wɒ́t ʃʊd ðə dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd ɒ́lt tɛ́kst bij?
trans_Explanation: ɒ́lt tɛ́kst (ɔltɜ́rnətɪv tɛ́kst) ɪz ə ʃɔ́rt tɛ́kst ɪkwɪ́vələnt əv ən ɪ́mɪdʒ ðæt skríjn ríjdərz ǽnnawns, ənd WCAG səksɛ́s krajtɪ́rijən 1.1.1 (nɒ́n-tɛ́kst kɒ́ntɛnt) rɪkwájərz ɪt fɔr ɪnfɔ́rmətɪv ɪ́mɪdʒɪz. ɡʊ́d ɒ́lt tɛ́kst kənvéjz ðij ɪ́mɪdʒɪz pɜ́rpəs ənd kíj kɒ́ntɛnt ɪn kɒ́ntɛkst, júwʒəwəlij ɪn ə sɛ́ntəns ɔr lɛ́s (ə kɒ́mən ɡə́ɪdɛlɪn ɪz ə́ndər əbáwt 125 kǽrəktərz), ənd əvɔ́jdz rɪdə́ndənt fréjzɪz sə́tʃ æz 'ɪ́mɪdʒ əv' ɔr kíjwɜ̀rd stə́ffɪŋ. dɛ́krətɪv ɪ́mɪdʒɪz ðæt ǽd nów ɪ̀nfərméjʃən ʃʊd həv ən ɛ́mptij ɒ́lt ǽtrɪbjùwt sów skríjn ríjdərz skɪ́p ðɛm. wɛ́n dʒɛ́nərèjtɪŋ ɒ́lt tɛ́kst wɪð ə mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəl, ɡɪ́v ɪt ðə péjdʒ kɒ́ntɛkst ənd ɔ́dijəns, ənd həv píjpəl rɪvjúw ɪ́mɪdʒɪz wɛ́r ǽkjərəsij mǽtərz.

Question: A report includes a complex chart whose data can't be conveyed in short alt text. What should you generate in addition to the alt text?
Explanation: An extended image description (long description) provides the full information of a complex image, such as a chart, diagram, map or infographic, in text near the image or linked from it, while short alt text identifies the image and points to the longer description. For charts, the extended description typically states the chart type, axes, key values, trends and conclusions, or provides the underlying data table. Multimodal models can draft these descriptions, and a structured prompt (summary first, then details) aligned with WCAG and your style guide improves consistency. Generated descriptions should be reviewed for accuracy, because errors in data descriptions mislead screen reader users.
trans_Question: ə rɪpɔ́rt ɪnklúwdz ə kəmplɛ́ks tʃɑ́rt húwz déjtə kǽnt bij kənvéjd ɪn ʃɔ́rt ɒ́lt tɛ́kst. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw dʒɛ́nərèjt ɪn ədɪ́ʃən tə ðij ɒ́lt tɛ́kst?
trans_Explanation: ən ɪkstɛ́ndɪd ɪ́mɪdʒ dɪskrɪ́pʃən (lɔ́ŋ dɪskrɪ́pʃən) prəvájdz ðə fʊ́l ɪ̀nfərméjʃən əv ə kəmplɛ́ks ɪ́mɪdʒ, sə́tʃ æz ə tʃɑ́rt, dájəɡræ̀m, mǽp ɔr ɪ́nfɒɡræfɪk, ɪn tɛ́kst nɪ́r ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ ɔr lɪ́ŋkt frəm ɪt, wájl ʃɔ́rt ɒ́lt tɛ́kst ajdɛ́ntɪfàjz ðij ɪ́mɪdʒ ənd pɔ́jnts tə ðə lɔ́ŋɡər dɪskrɪ́pʃən. fɔr tʃɑ́rts, ðij ɪkstɛ́ndɪd dɪskrɪ́pʃən tɪ́pɪkəlij stéjts ðə tʃɑ́rt tájp, ǽksijz, kíj vǽljuwz, trɛ́ndz ənd kənklúwʒənz, ɔr prəvájdz ðij ə̀ndərlájɪŋ déjtə téjbəl. mə̀ltijmówdəl mɒ́dəlz kən drǽft ðijz dɪskrɪ́pʃənz, ənd ə strə́ktʃərd prɒ́mpt (sə́mərij fɜ́rst, ðɛ́n dɪtéjlz) əlájnd wɪð WCAG ənd jɔr stájl ɡájd ɪ̀mprúwvz kənsɪ́stənsij. dʒɛ́nərèjtɪd dɪskrɪ́pʃənz ʃʊd bij rɪvjúwd fɔr ǽkjərəsij, bɪkɒ́z ɛ́rərz ɪn déjtə dɪskrɪ́pʃənz mɪ́slɛd skríjn ríjdər júwzərz.

Question: You need to extract custom visual attributes, such as product category, dominant color and whether a logo is visible, from product photos as structured fields by using Content Understanding. What should you create?
Explanation: A custom image analyzer in Azure Content Understanding is an analyzer you create on top of the prebuilt-image base analyzer with your own field schema, so each image returns structured fields, such as product category, dominant color or whether a logo is visible, as JSON. Image fields typically use the generate method (the model produces a value from visual evidence) or the classify method (the model picks a value from an enum), and each field's name, type and description act as instructions. You create the analyzer with a PUT to /contentunderstanding/analyzers/{analyzerId} and run it with POST .../analyzers/{analyzerId}:analyze, a long-running operation that you poll for the result. Content Understanding uses Foundry model deployments (a completion model and an embedding model) that you configure as defaults for the resource.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə ɪkstrǽkt kə́stəm vɪ́ʒwəl ǽtrɪbjùwts, sə́tʃ æz prɒ́dəkt kǽtɪɡɔ̀rij, dɒ́mɪnənt kə́lər ənd wɛ́ðər ə lówɡow ɪz vɪ́zɪbəl, frəm prɒ́dəkt fówtòwz æz strə́ktʃərd fíjldz baj júwzɪŋ kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw krijéjt?
trans_Explanation: ə kə́stəm ɪ́mɪdʒ ǽnəlàjzər ɪn ǽʒər kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ ɪz ən ǽnəlàjzər juw krijéjt ɒn tɒ́p əv ðə prebuilt-image béjs ǽnəlàjzər wɪð jɔr ówn fíjld skíjmə, sów íjtʃ ɪ́mɪdʒ rɪtɜ́rnz strə́ktʃərd fíjldz, sə́tʃ æz prɒ́dəkt kǽtɪɡɔ̀rij, dɒ́mɪnənt kə́lər ɔr wɛ́ðər ə lówɡow ɪz vɪ́zɪbəl, æz JSON. ɪ́mɪdʒ fíjldz tɪ́pɪkəlij júws ðə dʒɛ́nərèjt mɛ́θəd (ðə mɒ́dəl prədúwsɪz ə vǽljuw frəm vɪ́ʒwəl ɛ́vɪdəns) ɔr ðə klǽsɪfàj mɛ́θəd (ðə mɒ́dəl pɪ́ks ə vǽljuw frəm ən íjnəm), ənd íjtʃ fíjldz néjm, tájp ənd dɪskrɪ́pʃən ǽkt æz ɪ̀nstrə́kʃənz. juw krijéjt ðij ǽnəlàjzər wɪð ə PUT tə /contentunderstanding/analyzers/{analyzerId} ənd rə́n ɪt wɪð POST .../analyzers/{analyzerId}:analyze, ə lɔ́ŋ-rə́nɪŋ ɒ̀pəréjʃən ðət juw pówl fɔr ðə rɪzə́lt. kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ júwzɪz fáwndrij mɒ́dəl dɪplɔ́jmənts (ə kəmplíjʃən mɒ́dəl ənd ən ɪmbɛ́dɪŋ mɒ́dəl) ðət juw kənfɪ́ɡjər æz dɪfɔ́lts fɔr ðə ríjsɔrs.

Question: For a RAG index over a large photo collection, you need a ready-made Content Understanding analyzer that produces a natural language description of each image for search, without defining fields. Which analyzer should you use?
Explanation: prebuilt-imageSearch is a Content Understanding RAG analyzer that turns an image into search-ready content, chiefly a detailed natural language description, which you can embed and index for retrieval. The RAG analyzers (prebuilt-documentSearch, prebuilt-imageSearch, prebuilt-audioSearch and prebuilt-videoSearch) need no schema and produce output optimized for grounding agents and search indexes. Base analyzers such as prebuilt-image and prebuilt-video are the starting points for custom analyzers with your own fields. Descriptions make images findable by text queries, and they can be combined with multimodal embeddings for image similarity search.
trans_Question: fɔr ə RAG ɪ́ndɛks ówvər ə lɑ́rdʒ fówtòw kəlɛ́kʃən, juw níjd ə rɛ́dij-méjd kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ ǽnəlàjzər ðæt prədúwsɪz ə nǽtʃərəl lǽŋɡwɪdʒ dɪskrɪ́pʃən əv íjtʃ ɪ́mɪdʒ fɔr sɜ́rtʃ, wɪðáwt dɪfájnɪŋ fíjldz. wɪ́tʃ ǽnəlàjzər ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: prebuilt-imageSearch ɪz ə kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ RAG ǽnəlàjzər ðæt tɜ́rnz ən ɪ́mɪdʒ ɪ́ntə sɜ́rtʃ-rɛ́dij kɒ́ntɛnt, tʃíjflij ə dɪtéjld nǽtʃərəl lǽŋɡwɪdʒ dɪskrɪ́pʃən, wɪ́tʃ juw kən ɪmbɛ́d ənd ɪ́ndɛks fɔr rɪtríjvəl. ðə RAG ǽnəlàjzərz (prebuilt-documentSearch, prebuilt-imageSearch, prebuilt-audioSearch ənd prebuilt-videoSearch) níjd nów skíjmə ənd prədúws áwtpʊ̀t ɒ́ptɪmàjzd fɔr ɡráwndɪŋ éjdʒənts ənd sɜ́rtʃ ɪ́ndɛksɪz. béjs ǽnəlàjzərz sə́tʃ æz prebuilt-image ənd prebuilt-video ɑr ðə stɑ́rtɪŋ pɔ́jnts fɔr kə́stəm ǽnəlàjzərz wɪð jɔr ówn fíjldz. dɪskrɪ́pʃənz méjk ɪ́mɪdʒɪz fɪ́ndəbəl baj tɛ́kst kwɪ́rijz, ənd ðej kən bij kəmbájnd wɪð mə̀ltijmówdəl ɪmbɛ́dɪŋz fɔr ɪ́mɪdʒ sɪ̀mɪlɛ́rɪtij sɜ́rtʃ.

Question: You need to prepare long training videos for RAG, with a transcript, key frames and a description for each scene, without defining custom fields. Which Content Understanding analyzer should you use?
Explanation: prebuilt-videoSearch is a Content Understanding RAG analyzer for video that outputs search-ready content: a transcript in WebVTT format, ordered key frames, and segments with natural language descriptions that combine visual and speech context. Video analysis first extracts content (transcription with speaker diarization, shot detection and key frames) and then uses a generative model for segment descriptions and any custom fields. The analyzer samples about one frame per second, resized to 512 x 512 pixels, so very brief events or small on-screen text can be missed, and only speech is transcribed, not music or sound effects. Its output can be chunked by segment and indexed in Azure AI Search for video RAG.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə prɪpɛ́r lɔ́ŋ tréjnɪŋ vɪ́dijòwz fɔr RAG, wɪð ə trǽnskrɪ̀pt, kíj fréjmz ənd ə dɪskrɪ́pʃən fɔr íjtʃ síjn, wɪðáwt dɪfájnɪŋ kə́stəm fíjldz. wɪ́tʃ kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ ǽnəlàjzər ʃʊd juw júws?
trans_Explanation: prebuilt-videoSearch ɪz ə kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ RAG ǽnəlàjzər fɔr vɪ́dijòw ðæt áwtpʊ̀ts sɜ́rtʃ-rɛ́dij kɒ́ntɛnt: ə trǽnskrɪ̀pt ɪn WebVTT fɔ́rmæ̀t, ɔ́rdərd kíj fréjmz, ənd sɛ́ɡmənts wɪð nǽtʃərəl lǽŋɡwɪdʒ dɪskrɪ́pʃənz ðæt kɒ́mbajn vɪ́ʒwəl ənd spíjtʃ kɒ́ntɛkst. vɪ́dijòw ənǽlɪsɪs fɜ́rst ɪ́kstræ̀kts kɒ́ntɛnt (træ̀nskrɪ́pʃən wɪð spíjkər dàjərɪzéjʃən, ʃɒ́t dɪtɛ́kʃən ənd kíj fréjmz) ənd ðɛ́n júwzɪz ə dʒɛ́nərətɪv mɒ́dəl fɔr sɛ́ɡmənt dɪskrɪ́pʃənz ənd ɛ́nij kə́stəm fíjldz. ðij ǽnəlàjzər sǽmpəlz əbáwt wə́n fréjm pə́r sɛ́kənd, rɛ́sɪzɪd tə 512 x 512 pɪ́ksəlz, sów vɛ́rij bríjf ɪvɛ́nts ɔr smɔ́l ɒn-skríjn tɛ́kst kən bij mɪ́st, ənd ównlij spíjtʃ ɪz trǽnskrɪbɪd, nɒ́t mjúwzɪk ɔr sáwnd ɪfɛ́kts. ɪts áwtpʊ̀t kən bij tʃə́ŋkt baj sɛ́ɡmənt ənd ɪ́ndɛkst ɪn ǽʒər AI sɜ́rtʃ fɔr vɪ́dijòw RAG.

Question: News broadcasts must be split into one segment per news story, ignoring ads, with fields extracted for each story. How should you configure the Content Understanding video analyzer?
Explanation: Video segmentation in Content Understanding divides a video into logical segments before field extraction: with enableSegment set to false, the whole video is one segment, and with enableSegment set to true, contentCategories describe in natural language how to segment (for example one segment per news story, excluding ads), producing segments from seconds to minutes long. Each segment gets its own field values from the field schema, using methods such as generate and classify (with an enum of allowed values). Segmentation uses the generative model, so it consumes tokens even when no fields are defined. Shots and key frames are lower-level outputs, and camera shot times are returned when returnDetails is true.
trans_Question: núwz brówdkæsts məst bij splɪ́t ɪ́ntə wə́n sɛ́ɡmənt pə́r núwz stɔ́rij, ɪɡnɔ́rɪŋ ǽdz, wɪð fíjldz ɪkstrǽktɪd fɔr íjtʃ stɔ́rij. háw ʃʊd juw kənfɪ́ɡjər ðə kɒ́ntɛnt ə̀ndərstǽndɪŋ vɪ́dijòw ǽnəlàjzər?

Question: A media archive needs video insights such as face identification, celebrity recognition, brands and topics, with a ready-made portal and widgets. Which service fits best?
Explanation: Azure AI Video Indexer is a video analytics service that extracts insights such as transcripts and translations, faces and celebrities, labels, on-screen text (OCR), scenes, shots, keyframes, topics and brands, and offers a web portal, embeddable widgets and an API for media archives. Face identification and celebrity recognition are Limited Access features that require approval. Content Understanding is the generative AI option for custom per-segment fields and RAG-ready video output, while Video Indexer provides a broad set of prebuilt media insights. For LLM-based question answering over video, you can also sample frames and send them, with the transcript, to a multimodal model.
trans_Question: ə míjdijə ɑ́rkàjv níjdz vɪ́dijòw ɪ́nsàjts sə́tʃ æz féjs ajdɛ̀ntɪfɪkéjʃən, səlɛ́brətij rɛ̀kəɡnɪ́ʃən, brǽndz ənd tɒ́pɪks, wɪð ə rɛ́dij-méjd pɔ́rtəl ənd wɪ́dʒəts. wɪ́tʃ sɜ́rvɪs fɪ́ts bɛ́st?

Question: Invoices must be checked against the terms of a supplier contract, using multi-step reasoning across both documents. Which Content Understanding mode should you use?
Explanation: Pro mode in Azure Content Understanding, introduced with the 2025-05-01-preview API, is designed for complex document scenarios that need multi-step reasoning, multiple input documents and reference data supplied at analyzer creation, such as checking invoices against a contract to find inconsistencies. It supports only document content, uses classify and generate fields rather than extract fields, and doesn't return confidence scores or grounding. Standard mode, the default, handles documents, images, audio and video, minimizes cost and latency, and returns grounding and confidence scores for extracted fields. Choose standard mode for broad extraction and pro mode for cross-document validation and inference.

Question: You need extracted invoice fields with confidence scores and source locations so that low-confidence values go to human review. Which Content Understanding mode should you use?
Explanation: Standard mode is the default Content Understanding processing mode for documents, images, audio and video: it extracts, classifies or generates fields from a single input at low cost and latency, and for document fields it returns grounding (the source location of each value) and confidence scores. Confidence scores let you send low-confidence fields to human review and accept high-confidence ones automatically, and grounding lets reviewers jump straight to the evidence. Standard mode also supports labeled training examples for documents to improve accuracy. Pro mode adds cross-document reasoning and reference data but doesn't return confidence scores or grounding.

Question: In Content Understanding pro mode, where do you provide a contract and price list that the analyzer consults to validate each incoming invoice?
Explanation: Reference data in Content Understanding pro mode is a set of documents supplied when you create an analyzer, such as a contract, price list or policy, that the analyzer consults at analysis time to validate or enrich extracted information. It enables checks such as whether an invoice's line items match agreed prices, using multi-step reasoning that breaks the task into simpler questions. The service works in lookup mode against reference documents, so data that must be recovered exhaustively should be included in the input set instead. Pro mode also accepts multiple input documents per analysis, which supports cross-file analysis such as reconciling an invoice, a purchase order and a receipt.

Question: A factory must locate and count specific defect types on product images, returning bounding boxes, by training on its own labeled images. What should you build?
Explanation: Object detection is a computer vision task that finds instances of objects in an image and returns each one's class label, confidence and location as a bounding box, unlike image classification, which assigns labels to the whole image. For domain-specific objects such as product defects or components, you train a custom object detection model on your own labeled images, for example with Azure Machine Learning AutoML for images, which Microsoft recommends as the migration path from Azure AI Custom Vision (retiring on September 25, 2028). Multimodal LLMs can describe and roughly locate objects but are less precise and consistent for counting and pixel-accurate localization. Detection outputs can drive downstream rules, such as rejecting a part when a defect is found.
trans_Question: ə fǽktərij məst lówkèjt ənd káwnt spɪsɪ́fɪk díjfɛkt tájps ɒn prɒ́dəkt ɪ́mɪdʒɪz, rɪtɜ́rnɪŋ báwndɪŋ bɒ́ksɪz, baj tréjnɪŋ ɒn ɪts ówn léjbəld ɪ́mɪdʒɪz. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw bɪ́ld?
trans_Explanation: ɒ́bdʒɛkt dɪtɛ́kʃən ɪz ə kəmpjúwtər vɪ́ʒən tǽsk ðæt fájndz ɪ́nstənsɪz əv ɒ́bdʒɛkts ɪn ən ɪ́mɪdʒ ənd rɪtɜ́rnz íjtʃ wə́nz klǽs léjbəl, kɒ́nfɪdəns ənd lowkéjʃən æz ə báwndɪŋ bɒ́ks, ə̀nlájk ɪ́mɪdʒ klæ̀sɪfɪkéjʃən, wɪ́tʃ əsájnz léjbəlz tə ðə hówl ɪ́mɪdʒ. fɔr dowméjn-spɪsɪ́fɪk ɒ́bdʒɛkts sə́tʃ æz prɒ́dəkt díjfɛkts ɔr kəmpównənts, juw tréjn ə kə́stəm ɒ́bdʒɛkt dɪtɛ́kʃən mɒ́dəl ɒn jɔr ówn léjbəld ɪ́mɪdʒɪz, fɔr ɪɡzǽmpəl wɪð ǽʒər məʃíjn lɜ́rnɪŋ ɔ́towɛmɛl fɔr ɪ́mɪdʒɪz, wɪ́tʃ májkrəsɔ̀ft rɛ̀kəmɛ́ndz æz ðə majɡréjʃən pǽθ frəm ǽʒər AI kə́stəm vɪ́ʒən (rɪtájərɪŋ ɒn sɛptɛ́mbər 25, 2028). mə̀ltijmówdəl LLMz kən dɪskrájb ənd rə́flij lówkèjt ɒ́bdʒɛkts bət ɑr lɛ́s prɪsájs ənd kənsɪ́stənt fɔr káwntɪŋ ənd pɪ́ksɛl-ǽkjərət lòwkəlɪzéjʃən. dɪtɛ́kʃən áwtpʊ̀ts kən drájv dáwnstrìjm rúwlz, sə́tʃ æz rɪdʒɛ́ktɪŋ ə pɑ́rt wɛ́n ə díjfɛkt ɪz fáwnd.

Question: You need to list which component types appear in photos of circuit boards, with counts and rough positions, but you have no labeled training data and don't need precise coordinates. What should you use?
Explanation: Multimodal models such as GPT-4.1 or GPT-5 can identify objects and components in images zero-shot, with no training data, and return them as structured JSON (for example component type, count and a coarse location such as top left), which suits inventory checks, inspections and triage. Their spatial grounding, meaning precise coordinates and accurate counts of many small objects, is less reliable than a trained detector, so use custom object detection when you need pixel-accurate bounding boxes or consistent counts at scale. List the component types to look for, define how to report uncertain items and request high image detail for small parts. Validate outputs on a labeled sample before relying on them in production.
trans_Question: juw níjd tə lɪ́st wɪ́tʃ kəmpównənt tájps əpɪ́r ɪn fówtòwz əv sɜ́rkɪt bɔ́rdz, wɪð káwnts ənd rə́f pəzɪ́ʃənz, bət juw həv nów léjbəld tréjnɪŋ déjtə ənd dównt níjd prɪsájs kowɔ́rdɪnèjts. wɒ́t ʃʊd juw júws?
